records.name: Verde
records.summary: Studio Gang's 23-story, 254-unit rental tower at 1070 Bridgeview Way, the fourth and last Phase 1 building. Construction started March 2022, leasing began April 2024, residents moved in from June 2024 and the ribbon was cut September 3, 2024; 59 of its units are below market rate after a 2024 re-mix toward 90% AMI.

open_questions: Construction cost: not stated anywhere read; only the $116.2M Wells Fargo loan is on record.
Exact TCO date: the Port projected May then June 2024; no document read confirms the issued date.
Topping-out date: the Port's October 2023 memo only says it had topped out; no dated press item found.
Total square footage disagrees across sources (287,000 / 314,508 / 315,000); a permit record would settle it.

Images: no 'before' photo is hosted (until 2020 the parcel was the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot) and no rendering is hosted because the architects' renderings are not openly licensed; they are reachable through the architect sources listed here.

A Mapillary storefront photo of Ike's Love & Sandwiches (a sourced retail tenant, see the retail fact above) was hosted briefly and then removed: on review it read as too cluttered (a trash bin, a parked car and several pedestrians in front of the sign) to keep. Still on the shot list for a cleaner frame.

Arsicault Bakery's Verde shop is shown open on a March 11, 2025 release; it has not been re-confirmed since. BVNK's registration at 365 Toni Stone Xing (Fl 3) is not evidence of an operating office, so it is not shown as a tenant with an opening date.

records.name: Pier 48
names: Pier 48 Sheds A, B and C
records.summary: A 1928-30 reinforced-concrete finger pier with two transit sheds around an open 'valley' and Tudor/Gothic Revival bulkhead buildings, the southernmost contributor to the National Register-listed Port of San Francisco Embarcadero Historic District. The Mission Rock entitlements call for a Secretary of the Interior's Standards rehabilitation (261,000 gsf of production, restaurant, retail and exhibition uses); its planned anchor tenant Anchor Brewing closed in 2023, and today the pier is leased to the Giants' China Basin Ballpark Company for parking and events.

facts.value: Port of San Francisco (Board of State Harbor Commissioners when built)
1928-30; Shed C 1937-38; eastern third and Shed C rebuilt 1999-2000 after a 1996 fire

Sheds and bulkhead buildings by Board of State Harbor Commissioners engineers H.B. Fisher and B.P. Hudspeth under Chief Engineer Frank G. White; Tudor/Gothic Revival bulkhead buildings matching Pier 45
Healy-Tibbitts Construction Company (bulkhead wharf); L.M. King (transit sheds)
Contributor to the National Register-listed Port of San Francisco Embarcadero Historic District (listed 2006); California Historical Resource Status Code 1D
5.84 acres (HRE); 261,700 sq ft / 6.01 acres in the March 2012 Revised Proposal's parcel table

Pier substructure 369 ft wide, 610 to 635 ft long; bulkhead wharf 53 ft by 500 ft; originally to have been a much longer pier (the HRE gives no length), drastically shortened to 623 ft because of a mud-filled 'valley' 800 ft offshore; the 1924-26 Biennial Report quoted in the HRE announced Pier 48 as 610 ft long and 376 ft wide (the 1,200-ft figure in that passage is Pier 45's)
Two parallel transit sheds (A and B) on either side of an open-air 'valley' with remnant Belt Line Railway spur tracks, joined at the outer end by Shed C; berthing on three sides
261,000 gsf of light industrial, restaurant, retail and exhibition uses under the Secretary of the Interior's Standards (HRE); the EIR project table gives 242,500 gsf
Production and 'other' uses only under the Design Controls permitted land use table; residential, commercial, retail and parking-garage uses not permitted

Interim parking and special events under a 10-year lease to China Basin Ballpark Company, LLC (Giants affiliate); marketed by Giants Enterprises as a 200,000+ sq ft venue for up to 10,000 people, 24 Willie Mays Plaza
750 to 1,000 spaces, pending demand and valet operations (2019 Phase 1 submittal)

Not rehabilitated as of the Port's Mission Rock project page (read 2026-09-24), which still lists 'Historic rehabilitation of Pier 48' among what Mission Rock 'will be'; no Phase Submittal including Pier 48 found in the documents read. The DDA notes a rehabilitation may proceed 'based on' progress of the rest of the project and that historic tax credits are being explored
Historic rehabilitation of Pier 48 as part of the Mission Rock project

Whether the Port Commission Resolution 18-10 rent-credit terms for capital repairs were ever exercised.

records.notes: Pier 48 -- historic pier (two parallel steel-truss transit sheds, Shed A and Shed B, plus a connecting Shed C added 1937-38 at the bayward end; 261,000 gsf per the Historic Resource Evaluation, which also describes an open-air 'valley' between Sheds A and B, paved in asphalt with remnants of the Belt Line Railway spur tracks). Built 1928-30 (substructure begun 1928; bulkhead wharf completed July 17, 1929); a contributing resource to the Port's National Register-listed Embarcadero Historic District. IDENTIFICATION: this blklot has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll, but its real, surveyed shape (including the visible gap between sheds matching 'the Valley') matches Pier 48's footprint and location when overlaid on satellite imagery (Pier & Point's own overlay check, not a cited source). Marketed by Giants Enterprises as an event venue (corporate events, trade shows, concerts, conferences, galas, per its venue page) and leased to China Basin Ballpark Company for parking and special events (Board of Supervisors Resolution 43-18); the historic rehabilitation (to follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards) had not happened as of the Port's Mission Rock project page (read 2026-09-24), which still lists 'Historic rehabilitation of Pier 48' as part of what Mission Rock 'will be'. Anchor Brewing was slated as primary tenant for about 209,000 gsf of useable space (182,000 gsf brewery/distillery) spanning Sheds A, B and the valley (HRE); Anchor announced in July 2023 that it was ceasing operations (KQED), and in May 2024 its Potrero Hill brewery was bought by Hamdi Ulukaya's Shepherd Futures, which is working 'to help restart the brewery operations' (SF Standard); no source read states that the Pier 48 plan was formally cancelled. Recorded as 'existing' (a real, actively-used historic structure, not yet redeveloped per the masterplan) rather than 'complete' or 'planned'. LOT CORRECTED 2026-09-17: this row joined blklot 9900048, which DataSF's Assessor roll retired on 2020-06-12 (date_rec_drop); the live lot for the pier is 8719A001 (recorded the same day, active; DataSF Parcels acdm-wktn). Its shape also takes in the pier aprons -- the Design Controls' 'Pier 48 Apron' open space (Section 3.6) is therefore inside this record rather than drawn separately (Pier & Point's own reading of the lot shape).

open_questions: Construction cost: not stated in anything read.
Groundbreaking date: only The Registry's paywalled June 22, 2021 headline; the Port's December 2021 update confirms piles were done that year.
Square footage: four different figures across sources (272,770 / 281,639 / 295,000 / 313,952). The figure in this record's map notes (258,994 office + 13,773 retail) matches none of them exactly.
Address: 1090 Dr. Maya Angelou Lane vs 1051 3rd St vs 1089 3rd St (DataSF Assessor roll). Not resolved.
Lease terms and rents for the Warriors, Coinbase and Nvidia: undisclosed in every report read.

Images: no 'before' photo is hosted (until 2020 the parcel was the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot) and no rendering is hosted because the architects' renderings are not openly licensed; they are reachable through the architect sources listed here.
When Nvidia's lease commences: The Real Deal (Nov 21, 2025) says only that it 'is slated to occupy 45,000 square feet'; no commencement date appears in any source read.

Loeb & Loeb's page describes a 150,000 sq ft Building B lease for 'a leading cryptocurrency company' without naming Coinbase in its text (the name appears only in the page URL); the Coinbase attribution rests on Commercial Property Executive (May 2025).

MNT Studio's Mission Rock page lists the location with the 'opening class schedule' live and 'final week of founding memberships'; it has not been confirmed that the studio is open. Grey's Florals' August 2026 opening inside MNT's space has not been confirmed either.

records.name: Historic Building 12
records.summary: The 1941 Navy-built plate shop and mold loft at the heart of the World War II 'New Yard' (248 ft square, Aiken monitor roof), the first and so far only Phase 1 building delivered under Brookfield's Pier 70 DDA: lifted about ten feet against sea-level rise (12 ft per the contractor), rebuilt by Perkins&Will (architect) and Plant Construction (contractor) as a ground-floor market hall, second-floor maker studios and third-floor offices, and issued a temporary certificate of occupancy in January 2022. The DDA terms call for a 66-year, $1-a-year Port lease (no executed lease has been found); nearly 90% leased by August 2026, with two venture capital firms leasing the whole third floor (The Real Deal reports General Catalyst signed for it).

open_questions: Construction cost of the Building 12 rehabilitation itself: not stated anywhere; only the $237.4M Phase 1 total (Oct 2022) and the $150M infrastructure Notice of Completion figure exist.
Whether the 66-year Building 12 lease has been executed, and its date: the DDA sets the trigger, but no Port Commission lease approval for Building 12 was found on 2018-2026 agendas.

Tenants named in Port Item 11A are current as of its Aug 7, 2026 date only; the two third-floor venture capital firms are not named by the Port, and The Real Deal names General Catalyst as taking the entire third floor and Monograph Capital as having leased in 2024, so which firms occupy which space is unresolved.

records.name: Sophie Maxwell Building
records.summary: Eight-story, 105-unit, 100% affordable workforce housing building at 1212 Maryland St (corner of Humboldt St), the first building completed in the Potrero Power Station redevelopment; designed by Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects, built by Swinerton for Found Middle LP (Associate Capital / Fifth Space), completed August 2025, held its grand opening in October 2025 and began housing households at 50-110% AMI in November 2025.

facts.value: 1212 Maryland St, San Francisco, CA 94107 (corner of Humboldt St)
Found Middle LP (developer of Block 7B; affiliate of Associate Capital, now called Fifth Space); project sponsor for design review: California Barrel Company LLC
Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects (design and executive architect; certified SBA-LBE)
Plural (per the firm's own project page; collaborators LMS, CBG Engineers, RMA Irrigation)
Swinerton Builders
The John Stewart Company (JSCO)
105 (98 at the March 2022 design review approval; raised to 105 in the Q1 2023 revised site permit set)
104 restricted units plus 1 manager's unit; 100% affordable
50-110% AMI, averaging 80% AMI (Phase 1 application in 2020 assumed average 55% AMI; 2021 report 55%; 2022-2024 reports 80%)
70 studios, 21 one-bedroom, 14 two-bedroom (as built, per contractor); design review approval: 63 studios, 28 one-bedroom, 7 two-bedroom of 98
approximately 85 (design review memo; 84 per SF YIMBY; D4D maximum for the 7B lot is 85 ft)
83,000 total (design review plan sheet G0.1A); residential area 80,941 GSF (2024 compliance report)
approximately 1,820 (ground floor, cold shell)
residential (100% affordable workforce housing) with ground-floor retail, co-working space and rooftop deck
no vehicle parking; 99 Class I and 9 Class II bicycle spaces
LEED Gold certified; all-electric

First project to use the CalHFA Bond Recycling Program (recycled prior-year tax-exempt bonds) as the primary debt source; financing coordinated with MOHCD, OEWD and JPMorgan Chase; site infrastructure supported by an Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District (EIFD)
JPMorgan Chase (after pitching roughly six banks; negotiations took about seven months)

DA Housing Plan: 100% Affordable Housing Parcels are conveyed by the developer at no cost to the Affordable Housing Developer, in fee or by ground lease, under an Affordable Housing Conveyance Agreement (approved for Block 7B March 19, 2024)
104 100% Affordable Unit Credits toward the Phase 1 30% requirement (about 233 credits), the balance via in-lieu fee credits
about 90% leased as of July-August 2026; about eight applicants per unit at opening
85 for the 7B lot (Block 7 overall: 240-ft highrise tower permitted)
Sophenia 'Sophie' Maxwell, District 10 Supervisor 2001-2011, who led the effort to close the Potrero power plant (closed 2011)
AIA California 2026 Design Award, Citation

open_questions: Bond amount and issuer for the CalHFA bond-recycling debt (and whether CSCDA or another conduit was involved): looked in the Port memo 10A, the four DA annual reports, the Chronicle (Oct 2023, Aug 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025), SF YIMBY, Hoodline; no dollar amount for the bonds is stated anywhere.

Total development cost: only Hoodline (Dec 2025, citing the Chronicle) gives '$50 million'; the Standard gives $670,000 per unit (105 x 670,000 = about $70M). The two figures are inconsistent and neither is from a primary document.

Temporary Certificate of Occupancy / First Certificate of Occupancy date: the Port memo says construction was 'completed in August 2025'; no TCO date found. The 2025 DA annual report (due 2026) is not yet on the SF Planning page.

Construction start: the 2023 annual report and press give the groundbreaking ceremony as Oct 12, 2023 (site permit issued Oct 25, 2023), but the 2024 annual report says Found Middle 'commenced construction ... in June 2024' and the 2023 report says the construction contract 'commenced in 2024'. Both are recorded; the June 2024 date is probably the DA-defined commencement.

Design review approval date: the annual reports list Block 7B as 'Approved by Planning Department, 1.5.22; Planning Director Memo dated 3.2.22'. The signed approval letter is dated March 2, 2022; the Jan 5, 2022 event is not otherwise documented.

Parcel: the design review memo lists parent lots 4175/017, 4175/002, 4232/001 and 4232/006; the block/lot 4232020 used here must post-date the Phase 1 Final Map (recorded July 26, 2022). No document reviewed states the new lot number; 'Lot 10' appears on the LMS plan sheets ('Block 7B - Lot 10').

Land conveyance to Found Middle: the DA Housing Plan requires conveyance at no cost in fee or by ground lease; the approved Affordable Housing Conveyance Agreement (March 19, 2024) was not among the documents reviewed, so fee vs. ground lease and term are unknown.

Lottery: the SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says a random lottery would be held later that month, while the May 2025 Housing Plan amendment exempts 100% affordable projects that receive no direct City money from the MOHCD lottery. Whether Sophie Maxwell is a 'City Financed Unit' project is not stated.
Unit mix as built: Swinerton (contractor's own material) gives 70/21/14; the 2022 approval gives 63/28/7 of 98. No City document with the 105-unit mix was found.
Hoodline (Dec 6, 2025) calls it a 'six-story building'; every other source says eight stories. Treated as an error in Hoodline.

No hostable 'now' photograph found: Wikimedia Commons searches for 'Sophie Maxwell Building', 'Potrero Power Station' and 'Dogpatch Power Station' returned no photo of the building (only pre-2011 power plant images). Henrik Kam's photos (SF YIMBY, AIA CA) are not openly licensed; linked only.

Citizen Portal's AI-generated summary of the Oct 2025 opening mentions six Homeless Prenatal Program families among the first residents and 'resident parking'; not used because it is machine-generated from a video and the design approval states no vehicle parking.

Whether Fifth Space's Essential Housing Fund closed and the Sophie Maxwell Building was contributed to it: the SF Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) said the fund was expected to close the following week; searches on 2026-09-29 found no later source confirming either.

Exact day residents first moved in: ABC7 (Oct 20, 2025) gave Nov 1 as the planned date and Hoodline (Dec 6, 2025) says only that first families began moving in during November; no source gives the actual day.

records.notes: MB4E -- 398-unit, 100% affordable (30-95% AMI per SF YIMBY, 2025) two-phase development (Phase I: 165 units/16 stories on the southern half of the block, facing China Basin and Third Streets; Phase II: 233 units/23 stories on the northern half, facing Mission Rock and Third Streets, per the 2026 OCII Notice of Exemption), plus an approximately 1,253 sq ft ground-floor retail space (same Notice of Exemption; SF YIMBY's 2025 article gave 1,280 sq ft), at 1290 3rd St (DataSF Parcels) on the block bounded by Mission Rock, Third and China Basin Streets. Developed by Curtis Development + Bayview Senior Services under SF's Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (OCII) in the Mission Bay South Redevelopment Project Area. No cited source describes it as part of, or administratively separate from, the Giants/Tishman Speyer Mission Rock masterplan (the Verde/Canyon rows above), though it sits next to that area and faces a street named Mission Rock St. Site use: Pier & Point observed a surface parking lot here on the ground (2026-09-13); no cited document states this. Construction: the developer's project site (mb4e.com) lists Phase I construction start Q1 2027 and Phase II Q1 2028, pending financing, with bid packages through Q3 2026; SF's Spring 2026 development forecast (media.api.sf.gov/documents/Spring_2026_DEV_Forecast.pdf) was cited for the same schedule but could not be read on 2026-09-29. Not under vertical construction as of 2026-09-13 (Pier & Point's own observation), despite likely visible fencing/site-prep activity. NOTE: added after Pier & Point's own on-the-ground observation of this lot; the other facts were checked against OCII commission exhibits, the Notice of Exemption and DataSF parcel records. (mb4e.com; sfyimby.com/2025/06/renderings-revealed-for-23-story-affordable-housing-in-mission-bay-san-francisco.html; media.api.sf.gov/documents/Spring_2026_DEV_Forecast.pdf)

open_questions: Has the OCII Commission voted on the MOU? Not shown by any source read: it was absent from the September 1, 2026 agenda (which announces the next regular meeting for September 15, 2026). No agenda, minutes or cancellation notice for September 15 was read; re-check before relying on this.
No named developer was found for either half of the split parcel; OCII's presentation references a forthcoming RFP for the affordable-housing half only.

No firm entitlement timeline beyond 'environmental review, late 2026' was found; subsequent steps (Owner Participation Agreement amendment, Redevelopment Plan amendment, Design for Development, Blocks 11-12 Major Phase application, subdivision map) are listed only as an ordered sequence with no dates.

No press coverage (SF Chronicle, SF Standard, Mission Local, Potrero View, YIMBY) of the 2026 MOU proposal was found; all substantive detail traces back to OCII's own documents, so this remains a thin, single-source record pending independent coverage.
No cost, budget or subsidy figures for Block 12 West were found in any source reviewed.

No construction-start or completion date has been found for either half of the subdivided parcel, and no expected-completion milestone has been added (as of 2026-09-20): the only whole-plan-area date in OCII's own documents is the Mission Bay South Redevelopment Plan's own 30-year administrative term (Ordinance No. 335-98, effective from Nov 2, 1998), which sets when OCII's authority under the Plan ends, not when a project actually gets built -- using it as a stand-in for a construction-buildout target would misrepresent an undeveloped, still-unentitled parcel as complete in about two years. It stays on the timeline's open-ended 2038+ placeholder until a real entitlement/construction schedule exists.

As of 2026-09-29, the site's current use is not stated in any source read (the OCII deck does not describe it; the 2015 plan says 'Vacant Lot/Land'); the earlier 'surface parking lot' wording had no source and was removed. The OCII CAC agenda link previously cited is no longer available (page not found); no record of the August 13, 2026 meeting itself was found.

records.name: Mission Bay South Block 9A
records.summary: 400 China Basin is a 148-unit, 100% affordable homeownership condominium development (8 stories, roughly 180,000 sq ft) in Mission Bay South, developed by China Basin Partners LLC (Curtis Development, Michael Simmons Property Development and Young Community Developers), designed by Mithun with associate architect YA Studio, and built by general contractor Nibbi Construction/Baines Group; it held a ribbon-cutting in late September 2025 (the project's press release announced a September 26 celebration, and SF YIMBY reported on October 2 that it had taken place the week before).

facts.value: 400 China Basin St (Mission Bay South Block 9A)
China Basin Partners LLC (also '350 China Basin Partners, LLC' in some OCII filings), a joint venture of Curtis Development, Michael Simmons Property Development and Young Community Developers
Mithun (architect of record), with associate architect YA Studio and landscape architect GLS
Nibbi Construction and Baines Group (named together as the general contractor)
148 (50 one-bedroom, 63 two-bedroom, 35 three-bedroom)
148 (100% of units are below-market-rate affordable homeownership)
Sale prices restricted to households earning 80-110% AMI, individual units priced at 75/85/95/105% of AMI; average affordability target about 90% AMI
180,063 total building area (129,712 residential) per OCII's 2021 filing; SF YIMBY's 2025 completion article cites approximately 200,000; the lot is 29,939 sq ft (0.69 acres) per OCII
~85 (zoning allowed up to 90 for the block)
100% affordable, permanently price-restricted homeownership condominiums (OCII Limited Equity Program)
State of California Infill Infrastructure Grant funding, OCII permanent/gap financing (forgivable loan), homebuyer sales proceeds, and a private construction loan from Goldman Sachs
Type I (concrete) construction, U-shaped 8-story building over a podium; foundation uses roughly 200-ft driven piles due to Bay Mud fill conditions

Targeted GreenPoint Rating of 195 in 2021 planning (above the RFP's 125 minimum); the project's own press release reports GreenPoint Rated Platinum certification; SF YIMBY reports all-electric power and rooftop solar
~34 spaces (0.23-0.25 cars/unit), unbundled from unit sales

records.name: Mission Bay School
records.summary: SFUSD's Mission Bay School is a four-story TK-5 campus at 1415 Owens St (about 81,800 sq ft per the design team; SF Standard says approximately 80,000) designed by DLR Group and built by McCarthy Building Companies, the design-build team SFUSD hired in 2022, under a reported $95.4 million construction contract funded by SFUSD's 2016 bond program (Proposition A). SFUSD held the ribbon cutting on August 6, 2026 and scheduled the first PreK/TK/K students for August 2026, making it Mission Bay's first public elementary school and SFUSD's first new school in about a decade.

Designed to be twice as sustainable as SFUSD's standard; Universal Design for Learning with movable glass partitions joining classrooms; ground-floor spaces with direct outdoor access; built-in classroom observation rooms for teacher training on each floor

A 'Mission Bay Hub' STEM program serving high schoolers from six SF high schools (SF Standard); described in 2022 as a STEM-focused linked learning hub preparing students for careers in health, bioscience and STEM fields, plus district professional-development space
Monette Benitez

records.notes: Kaiser Permanente San Francisco Mission Bay Medical Offices, 1600 Owens St -- a 9-to-10-story outpatient medical office building (sources disagree: STUDIOS Architecture's own project page says nine stories with 220,000 sq ft; Potrero View also says nine stories, while the DataSF Assessor tax roll says 10 stories and gives property_area 250,884 sq ft, likely including garage/below-grade area; Potrero View cites 200,000 sq ft) with primary care, OB/GYN, pediatrics, dermatology, orthopedics, optical and occupational health -- no emergency department. Built speculatively by developer Alexandria Real Estate Equities, architect STUDIOS Architecture, design-build general contractor Whiting-Turner; STUDIOS Architecture's project page says Kaiser Permanente "purchased the project" from that speculative development; the sale date, price and seller are not stated in any source read here. Completed 2016 (STUDIOS); Potrero View reported in February 2016 that the offices would open in March 2016 (a pre-opening announcement; no post-opening source read). LEED rating also disputed (STUDIOS claims Platinum; Potrero View says Gold) and left unresolved. Blklot 8709020 confirmed via DataSF's Assessor Parcels dataset and Historical Secured Property Tax Roll (property_location '1600 OWENS ST', use_code COMO/property_class OMD, year_property_built 2016); zoning_district 'MISSION BAY REDEVELOPMENT' (MB-RA) in DataSF's Assessor parcel data confirms the Mission Bay South project area.

open_questions: Precise completion month not found -- David Baker Architects' own project page gives only 'Completed 2017'.

DataSF's Assessor tax roll records no year_property_built for this parcel (blklot 8711226), consistent with this record's map note; the 2017 completion year rests on the architect's project page rather than a public assessor or permit record.

A November 2016 UCSF news item describes the building as still welcoming applications ahead of opening, consistent with a 2017 (rather than the originally targeted September 2016) completion, but doesn't itself give a specific opening date.
Blue Bottle Coffee's confirmed opening date is not given by any source found (status: announced).

records.notes: Five88 (Mission Bay South Block 7 West), 588 Mission Bay Blvd North -- 200 affordable apartments (SocketSite, Jan 2015), a four-story, ~230,000 sq ft mixed-use development with over 10,000 sq ft of ground-floor retail, 52 parking spaces and 306 bike spaces. Developed by Related California in partnership with Chinatown Community Development Center; architect David Baker + Partners. Targets households averaging up to 60% of Area Median Income, with 50 of the 200 units reserved with a preference for university/healthcare employees. SocketSite (Jan 2015) reported groundbreaking as expected in April 2015 with occupancy targeted for September 2016 (no report of the groundbreaking itself found); DataSF's Assessor roll (wv5m-vpq2) lists blklot 8711226 with year_property_built 2017 and 208 units on the 2023-2025 rolls (no year built or units on earlier rolls). DataSF's Building Footprints layer records no footprint of its own for this parcel (the one fragment intersecting it, mblr SF8711227, actually belongs to the neighboring Family House parcel at their shared boundary) -- confirmed visually against satellite imagery -- so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary directly, the same treatment as Mission Bay Block 6 East on this same block face.

DataSF's own Building Footprints layer only captures small fragments of this building's roof (a handful of small fragments, a few over 100 sq m, totaling well under the real footprint) rather than its full mass, confirmed visually against satellite imagery -- so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary (a single-building, single-parcel site) rather than the incomplete building-footprint layer, consistent with how every other real-parcel record here is drawn.

records.notes: 1450 Owens Street -- a 7-story, ~1-acre laboratory/office building at the Alexandria Center for Science and Technology's Mission Bay Megacampus, shell-and-core construction permit shown complete by DBI on 2025-05-19 (one trade-press report says the building came online in 2024; Bisnow says 2027 for the leased space; the sources disagree) (133,000 sq ft lab space, ~50,000 sq ft office, 2,600 sq ft ground-level retail per Commercial Property Executive/EurekAlert coverage of the building). Gladstone Institutes (whose own separate headquarters at 1650 Owens St, blklot 8709008, is already tracked) announced in March 2026 that it had secured 105,000+ sq ft of laboratory space here (occupancy expected in early 2027) for its data science and genomic immunology institutes, per Gladstone's own release and Bisnow (both dated 2026-03-25) -- this record tracks the real Alexandria-owned building/parcel, not a separate Gladstone-owned site. DataSF Assessor confirms blklot 8709017 at 1450 Owens St; the DataSF Building Footprints layer only captures small roof fragments (~688 sq m total) of this real ~4,607 sq m parcel, so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary directly, consistent with how this project handles other footprint-layer gaps (e.g. 1300 Fourth Street, Block 6E).

records.summary: 1470 Owens Street is a parking structure at Mission Bay, designed by Watry Design to serve multiple UCSF life-science buildings and the adjacent Kaiser Permanente Mission Bay Medical Offices. DataSF Assessor records and Watry Design's own project page both date its completion to 2020.

open_questions: Exact month/day of the 2020 completion is not sourced, only the year.

A separate WRNS Studio project page (wrnsstudio.com/projects/ucsf-parking-structure/) lists a 'UCSF Mission Bay Parking Structure' completed in 2012 -- this conflicts with the 2020 date and, given the address-specific Watry Design page and the Assessor's own parcel-tagged year both agree on 2020, is treated here as describing a different, earlier UCSF Mission Bay garage (there is more than one on the campus, e.g. the separately-listed Owens Street Garage at 1625 Owens St), not this parcel. Not independently confirmed which building the WRNS page depicts.

As of 2026-09-29, no source found dates the start of physical construction; the timeline carries the permit issue date (2018-10-03) and completion (2020) only. Watry Design's page lists its owner as 'Developer', so no source read names UCSF as the garage's owner.

WRNS Studio was earlier named as the designer; the only cited designer page (Watry Design) names Watry, and the WRNS 'UCSF Parking Structure' page has not been confirmed to be this garage, so WRNS is not stated here.

records.notes: 1470 Owens Street -- a parking structure serving multiple UCSF Mission Bay life-science buildings and the adjacent Kaiser Permanente Mission Bay Medical Offices, designed by Watry Design (its project page lists the owner only as 'Developer'; no source read names the garage's owner); garage entrance on Nelson Rising Street off Owens St (ParkChirp). Features a green-wall security screen and 25 EV charging spaces (per the designer's own project page); ParkChirp lists it as a parking facility. Identified by Pier & Point during a map review of open ground between already-mapped sites. DataSF's Assessor data (dataset wv5m-vpq2) lists blklot 8709019 at 1470 Owens St; this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary (the DataSF Building Footprints layer has no captured footprint at all for this parcel, likely a parking-structure gap in that dataset).

records.name: Prequel Park (Port sub-area)
names: Portions of Seawall Lot 349 and Pier 72
records.summary: Port-owned shoreline land (portions of Seawall Lot 349 and Pier 72; the DEIR's 1.6-acre 'Port sub-area' piece between the Power Station and the Bay, site of a potential recreational dock) leased to California Barrel Company for 66 years under Port Lease L-16662 for public open space. About 0.4 acre of the ~2-acre interim Prequel Park is to be built on it; the Port Commission amended the lease's permitted uses on Nov 18, 2025 (Resolution 25-70).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE ONLY -- digitized from an illustrative planning figure, not a surveyed record, then clipped to the real Port jurisdiction boundary on its water-facing side and opened to remove a spike artifact. The corrected centroid falls east of the real Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels, consistent with a bay-side location, and area now closely matches the EIR's stated ~1.6 acres for this piece. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly tens of meters on the land-facing sides (still smoothed into a convex outline over the true shape there), but the water-facing edge is now a real boundary, not hand-traced. Do not use for anything requiring exact boundaries. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Draft EIR Figure 2-2, "Project Site Sub-Areas and Ownership" (Potrero Power Station Mixed-Use Development Project Draft EIR, Case No. 2017-011878ENV, October 2018, p. 2-6), which shows the Port-owned "Port sub-area" (SF Port ownership, ~2.9 acres total in 3 non-contiguous pieces) at true scale with a north arrow and a 400-ft scale bar.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This land has no Assessor's Block/Lot number at all -- confirmed directly in the same Draft EIR, footnote 1, p. 2-5: "The Port sub-area, and City sub-area described below, are not assessed properties, and therefore do not have assigned Assessor's Block numbers." It would therefore not be expected to appear in DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset or to be matched to an Assessor block/lot (Pier & Point's inference from that footnote; a DataSF spatial query over the Port sub-area was not run to confirm).
notes.regulatory_context: Prequel Park is the ~2-acre interim open-space project (BCDC Application 2019.006.02, a non-material amendment for which BCDC received the application on June 19, 2025 and issued the amendment on June 26, 2026 per its permit application tracker; SF Port Commission Resolution 25-70, Nov 18, 2025, amending Lease L-16662 with California Barrel Company LLC) of which ~0.4 acres sits on this Port sub-area land near the future recreational dock. Construction targeted Q3 2026, public opening targeted Q3 2027 per the Port's Nov 14 2025 memo (Calendar Item 10A).

records.summary: Developer-owned portion of Prequel Park, the ~2-acre (2.75 acres per press) interim park designed with Heatherwick Studio around Unit 3 and the 300-foot Stack on the waterfront area entitled for a hotel; the Port memo of Nov 2025 targets construction in 2026 and opening in 2027, and the project's BCDC amendment was issued June 26, 2026. No source found confirms construction has started.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this polygon combines two different sourcing methods (how this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record) and has not been independently re-verified as a whole against satellite imagery. Its west edge is exact (shared vertices with Block 4/Humboldt Street Plaza/Block 9). Its east/shoreline edge inherits whatever accuracy Waterfront Park's own trace has -- treat it as a reasonable but not freshly-verified approximation of the real shoreline. This is the 'Power Station sub-area' complement to 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' -- together they approximate the full ~2-acre interim park project, though the true internal boundary between Port and Power-Station land has not been independently confirmed. The ~2-acre figure is stated in the Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 (Calendar Item 10A, p.3: Prequel Park 'will cover approximately 2 acres, of which approximately .4 acres will be located on the Premises'); the press gives 2.5-2.75 acres.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 (shoreline shown as 'Waterfront Park'); Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 (Calendar Item 10A) for the ~2-acre interim Prequel Park. notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This is Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something any cited source establishes.)
notes.regulatory_context: The Potrero Power Station-land portion of the ~2-acre Prequel Park interim open-space project (see 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' for the Port-jurisdiction portion and its own sourcing; the Port memo of Nov 14, 2025 puts about 0.4 acre on the Port premises). Per the Port memo the park is to include a multi-purpose lawn and sport courts, amphitheater seating, a quarter-mile walking and running track, water access and restrooms. Construction start is targeted for the third quarter of 2026 per the memo's p.4 (p.2 says the first quarter of 2026); no source confirms a start, so the status is 'planned'.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 21 (Substation No. 5, relocated)
records.summary: A circa-1900 steel-framed, corrugated-metal-clad shop with a double-gable monitor roof (101 ft by 76 ft, 10,172 sq ft), the only surviving Risdon Iron Works building and the earliest steel-clad structure in the district, later Bethlehem's Substation No. 5. One of the three historic buildings the DDA obliges Brookfield to rehabilitate: a 66-year lease at $1 a year must be signed within a year of completing the building on Parcel E1 (Phase 2C), so no rehabilitation has begun.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) as of 2026-09-17 -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 21: position rests on satellite imagery and the D4D's building figures (the NRHP nomination places Building 21 'just west of the Noonan Building'; the Port's 'fronting Slipways Commons' wording describes its planned position after a future relocation, not where it stands now) and its combined size (734.96 sq m) is within 4.4% of the 101ft x 75ft (~703.7 sq m) footprint given in D4D Figure 6.5.4. The match rests on position, size, and satellite corroboration, not an explicit building-number tag in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there). A small 49 sq m footprint ~9m away was not included. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). Superseded history: STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-13 -- this building's rehabilitation has not started as of the most recent primary sources found (see regulatory_context).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel), cross-confirmed against ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. This replaced, on 2026-09-17, a long chain of diagram- and text-based approximations (their sources are kept below for history). How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). Originally three converging real-world sources: (1) 2011 Port RFI "Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan" map (sfport.com/sites/default/files/FileCenter/Documents/939-Pier70_RFI_3-2-11_web.pdf, PDF p.11), a scaled map with real street labels (Illinois St, 20th St) showing Building 21 immediately adjacent to Building 12 near the historic core, annotated "BUILDING 21 PROPOSED TO BE RELOCATED"; (2) Aug 3 2017 Port Commission memo (sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Pier%2070%20Final.pdf, Exhibit F p.68): "Building 21 (Substation No. 5)... would be relocated approximately 75 feet to the southeast, and in its new location it would front Slipways Commons... sits directly next to the proposed new waterfront arts facility" (future tense: a planned relocation as part of the rehabilitation); (3) D4D Figure 3.6.1 "Illustrative Slipways Commons Plan" (p.56/PDF p.72), a scaled plan with a real 0-50-100ft bar and "MARYLAND ST" label, captioned "the historic node of Buildings 2, 12, and 21."
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in the Assessor parcel data and no distinct lot was identified for it: DataSF's Building Footprints carry the legacy lot id mblr SF4052001 for it and many other structures across central Pier 70, but blklot 4052001 was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn), and which current lot holds Building 21 was not established from a cited source. This feature therefore uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.regulatory_context: Building 21, originally Substation No. 5, is planned to be relocated approximately 75 feet to the southeast as part of its rehabilitation (Port Item 9B, Sept 2017: "would be relocated"; no source records that the move has happened), and is one of three historic structures (with Buildings 2 and 12) the Pier 70 Design for Development commits to rehabilitating per the Secretary of the Interior's Standards (Pier 70 D4D S6.6.1). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: an earlier version of this row marked it "complete," inferred (not directly cited) from Building 21 being grouped in the D4D's rehabilitation commitment alongside Buildings 2 and 12. Follow-up research found the Port's own 28-acre site page (sfport.com/projects-programs/pier-70-28-acre-site) describes Building 21's rehabilitation as still to come -- the page shows a rendering, not a photo, captioned "Rendering of Pier 70 Building 21," under a "Rehabilitation of three historic buildings" heading, implying a future vision rather than a completed project. This is corroborated negatively by the Port's own June 2025 project-update deck (sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/Pier%2070%20Update%20-%20June%202025%20v3.pdf), which shows Building 15's relocation and several Building 12 milestones but never mentions Building 21. Status corrected from complete to existing -- a standing historic structure, not yet rehabbed, with no confirmed construction timeline.

records.name: Mission Rock Block C
records.summary: A future Commercial Mixed Use block on 3rd Street south of Building B, entitled for a 190-ft building over a base with a maximum height of 90 ft on one side and 60 ft on the other with required ground-floor retail. Unbuilt: the Port's June 2026 Phase 2 update describes the site as a surface parking lot, with Phase 2 in pre-development and construction 'as early as 2027'; in 2023 a Port Commission resolution recited that Phase 2 was not currently financially feasible.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one: treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping this record from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Commercial Mixed Use only (no residential option) per the Design Controls' Land Use Plan (Figure 1.1) -- ground-floor retail required. Max building height 190 ft per Figure 6.2, confirmed exactly. Positioned south of Block B, fronting 3rd St to the west and the Shared Public Way (and Mission Rock Square beyond it) to the east. No construction-start source found; the Port's June 2026 Phase 2 update (Item 11A) describes the site as 'a surface parking lot' and puts Phase 2 construction 'as early as 2027'.

open_questions: No architect, program or unit/square-footage figure for Block C exists in any document read; the EIR's project-wide range is 972,000 to 1.4 million gsf of commercial space.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found in Port Commission agendas through February 2026; the block remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot (Lot A).
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block C. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) places Parcel C in Phase 2 in its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) and its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of May 2023 for completing Phase 2's horizontal Phase Improvements -- already elapsed with Phase 2 not begun, and the Outside Date for actual completion is left to a future Phase Schedule that was never approved (Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones). No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 2 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date for this block.

As of 2026-09-21: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding below that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (through Fall 2027 contractor procurement) and a 'potential' construction start as early as Summer/Fall 2027, but the memo explicitly frames 2027/2028/2029 as alternative scenarios depending on when the Developer secures anchor tenants, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.

open_questions: The Design Controls' Section 6.5.2 (Design Intent: Block D1) does say 'Block D1 marks the Mission Rock MUNI Metro Station'; located in the April 2018 text 2026-09-29.
Unit count and affordability for D1: none set; later phases may need more than 40% BMR to reach the project total after the 2025 Phase 1 cut.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found in Port Commission agendas through February 2026; the block remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot (Lot A).
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block D1. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) places Parcel D1 in Phase 2 in its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) and its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of May 2023 for completing Phase 2's horizontal Phase Improvements -- already elapsed with Phase 2 not begun, and the Outside Date for actual completion is left to a future Phase Schedule that was never approved (Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones). No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 2 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date for this block.

As of 2026-09-21: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding below that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (through Fall 2027 contractor procurement) and a 'potential' construction start as early as Summer/Fall 2027, but the memo explicitly frames 2027/2028/2029 as alternative scenarios depending on when the Developer secures anchor tenants, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.

records.name: Mission Rock Block D2
records.summary: The site of Mission Rock's only permitted stand-alone parking structure, a 100-ft-max garage on the Bridgeview Street side of Block D sized in the EIR at about 2,300 spaces (837,200 gsf) to replace Giants event parking. It is the one element the Port names as part of Phase 2, whose Garage Report was submitted in October 2022 before the phase was decelerated in 2023.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (see the mapping log): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. The D1/D2 line is a land-use zone boundary inside one Design Controls block, not a lot line; the Appendix marks Block D's parcel dimensions as illustrative. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m. D1/D2 split from Figure 1.1 (p.10) and the Block D standards sheet (Appendix p.190).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping this block from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Structured Parking per the Design Controls' Land Use Plan (Figure 1.1) -- a flat 100 ft max height (not a 90-110 ft range as sometimes described), with no upper/tower zone. Occupies the larger, eastern portion of the combined Block D parcel (D1 is the smaller residential tower at the 3rd St corner; see that entry). The April 2017 Draft EIR (Table 2-4) puts about 2,300 spaces in the above-grade parking structure on Block D (D2), with a further 700 in a below-grade garage under Mission Rock Square. The Central District Energy System was tentatively planned for Parcel A, not Block D, per a 2019 Mission Rock Partners submittal to the Port -- despite some secondary summaries placing it here.

open_questions: The Garage Report's actual space count and levels are not in the Port memo; the report itself was not located.
The shape's note that a 2019 submittal placed the district energy plant on Parcel A rather than Block D is confirmed by the July 2019 Phase 1 overview and the September 2019 budget memo.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found in Port Commission agendas through February 2026; the block remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot (Lot A).
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block D2. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) places Parcel D2 (the garage) in Phase 2 in its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) and its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of May 2023 for completing Phase 2's horizontal Phase Improvements -- already elapsed with Phase 2 not begun, and the Outside Date for actual completion is left to a future Phase Schedule that was never approved (Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones). No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 2 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date for this block.

As of 2026-09-21: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (through Fall 2027 contractor procurement) and a 'potential' construction start as early as Summer/Fall 2027, but the memo explicitly frames 2027/2028/2029 as alternative scenarios depending on when the Developer secures anchor tenants, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.

records.name: Mission Rock Block E
records.summary: A small Commercial Mixed Use block directly south of Mission Rock Square, capped at a flat 90 ft with no upper tower (Table 6.4 lists its upper-building controls as not applicable), meant to spill ground-floor uses into the square's gardens. No source read shows construction on it: the Port's June 2026 report still frames the site as a surface parking lot to be transformed, with Phase 2 construction possible as early as 2027.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2, fitted to 16 real lot corners with a typical (root-mean-square) misfit of about 0.7 m, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (how this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines.

records.name: Mission Rock Block I
records.summary: A flex block east of Mission Rock Square across Bridgeview Street, on Long Bridge Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard, developable as commercial (90 ft) or residential (120 ft) with an elevated sidewalk zone along the boulevard. No source read shows construction on it (the Port's June 2026 report: Phase 2, not yet begun, could start construction as early as 2027).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one: treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, document dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping this record from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.

open_questions: Whether Block J will be built residential or commercial has not been decided in any document read.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found in Port Commission agendas through February 2026; the block remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot (Lot A).
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block J. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) places Parcel J in Phase 4 in its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) and its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of February 2025 for completing Phase 4's horizontal Phase Improvements -- already elapsed with the earlier Phase 2 still not begun as of the October 2023 'not currently financially feasible' finding in this record's own milestones. No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 4 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date for this block.

The Design Controls approval is numbered Resolution 18-04 in the Port's January 26, 2018 staff report (a request) and Resolution 18-05 in its September 20, 2019 memo; the adopted resolution itself was not read.
Which blocks Phase 2 covers is not stated in the Port's June 5, 2026 report either, so this block's phase is not sourced from it.

records.name: Mission Rock Block K
records.summary: The smallest development block, a Residential Mixed Use site on Exposition Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard next to China Basin Park and the Pier 48 entry, capped at 120 ft. It was in the original Phase 1 but was swapped out for Parcel F in 2019 to bring about 100 more units into the first phase; no construction on Block K is reported in the sources read.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE but high confidence: every edge is a recorded DataSF lot line (the Assessor has not made Block K its own lot; it is still part of the China Basin Park lot 8719A005 in the most recent DataSF Assessor parcel data checked), and the Design Controls figure trace agrees with those lines within 1.3 m at every corner. Planned, unbuilt residential block (120 ft maximum height). ANGLE CHECK: one corner here is 12.3-12.6 degrees off square, beyond the 12-degree tolerance of Pier & Point's automated shape check. Every vertex of this polygon is a real, recorded DataSF Assessor lot corner (how this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record) -- the deviation is the real lot's own shape (Bridgeview Way's paseo lot 8719A007 and the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 meet the park lot 8719A005 at a corner that is not exactly square), not a shear or a misread trace. Accepted as a known exception.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor lot lines (lots 8719A005, 8719A007, 8719A010, 8719A003) bounding the lobe the plan's Block K occupies, cross-checked against Mission Rock Design Controls Figure 6.2 (p.151) and the Block K standards sheet (Appendix p.198).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Block K's land is still part of lot 8719A005 (China Basin Park), a lot recorded 2020-06-12 in DataSF's Assessor parcels (the DataSF Parcels dataset); the lot lines around it exist but the Assessor has not split K off in that data. Using lot 8719A005 would show the park and the block as one shape.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential Mixed Use, fronting China Basin Park and the Pier 48 entry along Terry A. Francois Blvd. Max height 120 ft -- tied for the lowest residential height limit on the site (Flex Blocks H, I and J also allow 120 ft if residential, Figure 6.2 p.151); the March 2012 Revised Proposal's narrative says 'the shortest residential tower would be on Block K facing Mission Rock Park,' preserving sightlines/stepping the skyline down toward the water. Originally slated for Phase 1 (with A, B, G) before a real, Port-confirmed 2019 swap with Block F -- the sponsors proposed changing Phase 1 from {A, B, G, K} to {A, B, G, F} to accelerate ~100 more units (~40 more affordable) and create a four-corner pedestrian intersection instead of a linear one; an interim-parking-preservation rationale sometimes cited for this swap is not supported by any source found.

records.name: Mission Rock Square
records.summary: The neighborhood's planned central park of about 1.1 acres (1.32 acres, 57,626 sq ft, in the March 2012 proposal), an urban green framed by Blocks E and F with a lawn, a plaza with an interactive spray ground, a cafe pavilion and a tree bosque with retail kiosks; the Design Controls require wind protection, public restrooms and preserved water views. The Draft EIR includes a 700-space garage beneath it. Unbuilt as of the Port's June 2026 Phase 2 update, which describes the site as a surface parking lot and puts Phase 2 in pre-development.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt public square) on the undivided remainder lot 8719A006. North edge is a recorded lot line (~0 m); the other three edges come from the Design Controls figure through a 0.7 m RMS transform (~1-3 m). Traced area 47,724 sf, smaller than the 57,626 sf the 2012 proposal gave -- the tracing is logged in this shape's data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). The July 2019 Phase 1 submittal planned 'two interim pedestrian plazas south of Parcels B and F'; no source read confirms that an interim plaza was built or where it sits, and the Port's June 2026 update describes the site as a surface parking lot.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls, Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151) and Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); north edge is Verde's recorded lot line (8719C001), south edge is Block E's traced north edge.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this square -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping each block from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this square touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Dedicated public open space (Design Controls Chapter 3, Section 3.3). Directly framed by Block F/Verde (north) and Block E (south), with the Shared Public Way (west) and Bridgeview Street (east) along its sides; Blocks B, C, I and J are also one street removed (Design Controls Figure 6.2). The Design Controls text states no acreage; the Port's January 2018 approvals report gives 1.1 acres ('a 1.1 acre neighborhood central gathering place called Mission Rock Square'), which matches this record's traced figure; the March 2012 Revised Proposal's parcel table gave 57,626 sf (1.32 ac) for an earlier, deeper layout.

open_questions: Which phase will deliver the square and whether the below-grade garage option survives: not stated in any Port memo read; the Phase 2 Garage Report was not located.
Cost of the square: none published. Phase 1's China Basin Park inland budget ($39-41M) is the only comparable figure in the Port memos.

The 1.1-acre figure in the 2018 approvals memo versus 1.32 acres in the March 2012 proposal is unexplained; the traced shape on this record's map is about 1.57 acres after clipping, per its own accuracy note.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Mission Rock Square. The DDA (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) was read in full: its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) assigns a Phase only to Development Parcels, not to the Square, which its Infrastructure Plan (DDA Exhibit B3, Section 1.8) instead ties to 'associated' Development Parcels -- here Block F (built in Phase 1) and Block E (Phase 3, per that record). Its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of August 2024 for completing Phase 3's horizontal Phase Improvements, already elapsed with the earlier Phase 2 still not begun as of the October 2023 'not currently financially feasible' finding in this record's own milestones. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. No later Port memo or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 3, for the square specifically, or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel A
records.summary: Phase 1 office parcel at 20th and Maryland Streets (per D4D Figure 6.4.2), entitled for roughly 350,000 gross square feet of commercial office over retail and underground parking; appraised at $66 million (reported February 2020) for a 99-year prepaid lease, but Brookfield declined to proceed in June 2020 and no vertical development has started. King Street Properties announced a life-science plan for it in 2023.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'), and no source read ties it to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcels include new lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019, without street addresses, but which lot (if any) is Parcel A's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see the mapping log) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17: this block's south edge fell ~11m short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery, leaving a strip of unclaimed vacant land between the block and the street -- consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors (Parcel E1's shape has the same root cause; see its mapping log). The diagram itself (Figure 6.4.2) shows this block's fill running right up to the street with no setback, so extended the two south vertices by 11m (measured in satellite imagery where the ground color changes to the real sidewalk, along 3 sample lines) to close the gap, matching the diagram's own convention rather than re-deriving the whole transform. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No source read ties this block to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor parcels include lots created for Brookfield's 28-acre district in 2019 (for example, Port Item 12B, Feb 2020, gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116, Lot 008), but Parcel A's own lot was not identified, so this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Commercial/life-science, 90 ft max / 6 stories per Figure 6.4.2. A revised design by Grimshaw with DES Architects + Engineers (356,400 sq ft, six stories, 90 ft) was reported by SF YIMBY in Oct 2021 with the refiled Development Agreement; King Street Properties announced in Feb 2023 a six-story, roughly 300,000 sq ft speculative life-science building on Parcel A (Bisnow). No source read links the Grimshaw design to King Street's plan, and no source read supports the earlier mention of a 2019 mass-timber design or a 365,000 GSF figure (removed 2026-09-29). No construction-start source found.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Whether the King Street Properties partnership is still in effect: the Port's June 2025 deck speaks of the life-science effort in the past tense ('prior to collapse of that industry') and the July 2026 Real Deal report describes a 300,000 sq ft office building, not a lab.
The Feb 2020 staff memo says Parcel A is entitled for ~350,000 GSF while Resolution 20-07's recital says ~240,000 GSF; which figure the DDA option actually carries is unresolved.
No source read supports an earlier (2019) mass-timber office design by Hacker Architects with Quezada Architecture that this parcel's map notes used to mention; it was removed on 2026-09-29.
Construction cost estimates for the office building: none found.

The Real Deal (July 16, 2026, citing the SF Chronicle) reports Brookfield is 'looking to start construction on a 300,000-square-foot office building if San Francisco's office recovery gains traction'; the report does not name a parcel, so it is not recorded as a Parcel A milestone.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel B
records.summary: Large commercial-office parcel on 20th Street at the waterfront, next to the ship-repair yard; 90 ft / six stories under the D4D. It is an option parcel of a later phase (Phase 3B in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan) and has no design, appraisal or construction record.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address) and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008, so which lot, if any, corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see the mapping log in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record)) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Office (Commercial-Office in all three D4D land-use scenarios, Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7; not residential/mixed-use), 90 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (6-story cap for commercial buildings per D4D Section 6.4.2, not the sometimes-cited '6-8 stories'). Phase 3B in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan (Port Item 11A, Exhibit A; the pump station site is shown as included in the earlier of 3A or 3B). No square footage for this parcel is stated in the D4D or Port Items 9B and 11A; a ~500,000 RSF figure previously recorded here came from an uncited leasing brochure and has been dropped. No construction-start source found.
