records.name: Pier 70 Parcel K North (PKN)
records.summary: The 1.5-acre former Port parking lot at 20th and Illinois Streets, sold in February 2019 to a TMG Partners / Presidio Bay Ventures joint venture under a Vertical DDA after a competitive offering, generating $24.2 million of land proceeds for the Pier 70 project. Planning approved a 65-ft, 245-unit for-sale condominium building over ground-floor retail (377,506 gsf, Handel Architects) in November 2019; the developers' pages call it fully entitled and Handel lists it 'In Design', and no construction start was found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (the developers' pages call it 'fully entitled' and Handel Architects lists it 'In Design'; no groundbreaking was found in any source read), and no source read identifies its Assessor lot: it was sold by the Port outright (Presidio Bay's page calls it 'the only privately-owned land in the Pier 70 Special Use District'), and DataSF's Assessor parcels list active P70-MU lots at about this location (for example lot 4110012 at 919 Illinois St, and lot 4110009 with no address), but which of them is Parcel K North's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (how the shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. This deliberately does NOT match today's satellite imagery of the parking lot -- this parcel's boundary represents the D4D's planned footprint, including '21ST ST (NEW)' and the '20th Street Plaza' open-space strip (mapped separately as the PKN Frontage Open Space), neither of which is built yet.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No source read identifies this parcel's Assessor lot. The Port sold Parcel K North outright in 2019 (Presidio Bay's page: 'the only privately-owned land in the Pier 70 Special Use District'), and DataSF's Assessor parcels list active P70-MU lots at about this location (for example lot 4110012 at 919 Illinois St, and lot 4110009 with no address), but which of them is Parcel K North's was not established, so this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential, 65 ft max / 6 stories. The Port's Parcel K North page describes a 65-foot, 377,506 square foot mixed use building containing 245 for-sale residential units over ground-floor retail, and Handel Architects lists 245 units (Presidio Bay's page says ±241 condominium homes and 411,273 sq ft). Developer is TMG Partners + Presidio Bay Ventures -- NOT Brookfield; Presidio Bay says it 'closed on the land acquisition from the Port of San Francisco in February 2019', and both developers' pages call the project 'fully entitled'. No groundbreaking was found in any source read (searched through 2026-09-29).

open_questions: The purchase price: the only figure found is the Port's '$24.2 million of land proceeds from the sale of Parcel K North in February 2019'; the executed Vertical DDA and the Budget and Legislative Analyst report attached to File 190055 were not opened.

No groundbreaking or building permit was found. Bisnow's June 2019 piece says TMG and Presidio Bay 'broke ground after recent purchase', which conflicts with the Port page's 2020-2021 design-and-permitting timeline and no groundbreaking was found in any source read; treat the 2019 claim as unverified. (The November 2025 Potrero View article about Pier 70 housing concerns Brookfield's site and does not mention Parcel K North, so it is not used here.)

Affordable housing on PKN: the 2017 memo calls the units market-rate and the 2026 report says condo projects pay an in-lieu fee toward the stand-alone affordable sites, while the Planning conditions reference Section 415 affordable units; the actual obligation is unresolved.
Unit and square-footage figures disagree between the Port page (245 units, 377,506 gsf) and the two developer pages (241 units / 411,273 sq ft; 275,000 sq ft residential).

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: Parcel K North was sold to a private developer in 2019 and sits outside the 28-Acre Project's DDA phasing plan, so no Development Agreement phase window applies to it; no PKN-specific schedule statement was found (the Port's November 2025 comment reported by Potrero View concerns Pier 70 generally), and the developers' own pages (TMG, Presidio Bay, Handel Architects) give no construction start or completion date, so this record stays undated.

Current build status of Parcel K North: the developers' pages (undated) call it 'fully entitled' and Handel lists 'In Design'; no source dated 2026 that names Parcel K North was found beyond Port Item 11A's mention of the 2019 sale.

records.name: PKN Frontage Open Space (20th Street)
records.summary: The roughly half-acre '20th Street Plaza' of the D4D open-space network (Section 3.10), the landscaped entry plaza on Parcel K North's 20th Street frontage at Illinois Street, designed as the gateway from Dogpatch to the Historic Core with an entry plaza, seating terrace and planted garden. The Port's Parcel K North project lists a 20th St/Illinois St plaza among the buyer's obligations; no source found reports it built (the Port's Parcel K North page schedule stops at 2020-2021 design and permitting).

notes.accuracy_caveat: LOW-MODERATE CONFIDENCE -- Figure 3.3.1 is an illustrative, non-dimensioned rendering (no scale-accurate internal boundaries, unlike the D4D's own numbered-parcel figures), so this is a simplified bounding-box trace, not a precise outline. The D4D does name this space: Section 3.10 '20th Street Plaza' (approximately 0.5 acre, with its own Figures 3.10.1-3.10.5); this record's title 'PKN Frontage Open Space (20th Street)' is the earlier location-based placeholder and is kept only as its identifier. Its south/east/west edges match PKN's newly-retraced boundary (see the mapping log in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record)); its north edge is now ground-truthed against the real 20th St centerline (6.8m curb offset) rather than Figure 3.3.1's own illustrative depth, which turned out to extend past the real street entirely. Resulting strip is real but thin (~305 sq m) -- narrower than the diagram's own illustrative rendering implies.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 3.3.1 - Illustrative Open Space Plan (p.51).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own identified. The plaza is on the Illinois & 20th Street Parcel (Block 4110/Lot 001 per Port Item 9B), which Port Resolution 17-52 has the Port merge with a vacated piece of Michigan St and subdivide into four parcels including its own 'Plaza Parcel'; that parcel is outside Brookfield's 28-Acre Site, so the earlier statement that it lies within Brookfield's site is withdrawn. The Plaza Parcel's Assessor lot has not been checked.
notes.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network: Section 3.10 '20th Street Plaza', approximately 0.5 acre, an entry plaza with a seating terrace and planted garden along Parcel K North's 20th Street frontage (Figures 3.10.1-3.10.5), shown on Figure 3.3.1 as landscaped open space. Port Item 9B (2017) lists the 20th Street Plaza among the infrastructure obligations retained for the adjacent Illinois Street Parcels.

records.name: Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space (Waterfront Terrace / Slipways Commons / Waterfront Promenade / Pier 70 Shoreline)
records.summary: The roughly five-acre waterfront park system of the Pier 70 D4D (Waterfront Terrace, Slipways Commons and Waterfront Promenade, Sections 3.5-3.7) plus the roughly 1,300-foot Pier 70 Shoreline (Section 3.8), to be built by the developer and owned by the Port. Phase 1 includes three acres of parks, but the DDA ties park completion to adjacent buildings and the Port's 2026 report says the Phase 1 parks will be built 'on a schedule that coincides with the delivery of adjacent vertical development', so none has been constructed.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE, AND KNOWINGLY UNSUBDIVIDED -- combines four D4D-named open spaces (Waterfront Terrace, Slipways Commons, Waterfront Promenade, Pier 70 Shoreline) into one polygon because the D4D figures used (3.4.1 and 6.4.2) show one continuous fill; the Port's SUD Land Use Plan (Exhibit A4-1, 03/13/2018) labels separate 'Open Space Segments' (WTP, SC-1, SC-2, WP-1, WP-2), which this polygon does not follow; do not treat this as a single named place. Total traced area (~4.0-4.3 acres before/after clipping) is a reasonable match to the D4D's own combined figures (a ~5.0-acre waterfront area covering the first three, plus part of a ~1,300-linear-foot shoreline) but is not a precise subdivision or survey. Programmatically traced from a diagram's fill color, not hand-verified vertex-by-vertex.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155); named/numbered per Figure 3.4.1 - Overview of Public Spaces (p.52).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space within Brookfield's 28-acre site. No source read ties it to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcels include lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019, without street addresses, but which lot (if any) covers this open space was not established.
notes.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3) -- specifically Sections 3.5 (Waterfront Terrace), 3.6 (Slipways Commons), 3.7 (Waterfront Promenade), and 3.8 (Pier 70 Shoreline, ~1,300 linear feet). Together with Building 12 Plaza/Market Square, 20th Street Plaza, Irish Hill Corner Plaza, and Irish Hill Playground, these comprise the D4D's total nine acres of public open space (Section 3.4).

records.name: Crane Cove Park
records.summary: Seven-acre Port of San Francisco waterfront park on the former shipyard shoreline between 19th and Mariposa Streets east of Illinois Street, built around historic Slipway 4 and a stabilized historic gantry crane, with a pocket beach and lawn, as a Blue Greenway waterfront park. Planned from 2011, built under a $17.8 million contract awarded to Gordon N. Ball in November 2018, and opened September 30, 2020 at a total cost of $36.7 million; the playgrounds and dog run followed on December 12, 2025.

notes.accuracy_caveat: HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon (not a hand trace or estimate), independently confirmed via its own leisure=park/operator/wikidata tags. Its area (~6.26 acres) is somewhat smaller than the ~7 acres given on the Port's project page (the Port's 2018 Item 12B calls it an 'approximately eight acre site') -- likely because this specific traced way covers the core landscaped park and not every associated feature (e.g. the boat launch apron or beach edge); not adjusted to match the citation since the citation isn't itself a boundary.
notes.digitized_from: OpenStreetMap (way 853562207, leisure=park, operator=Port of San Francisco, wikidata=Q108550863) -- a real, community-surveyed park boundary, not a diagram trace.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Port-owned public open space (OSM operator tag: Port of San Francisco). DataSF's Assessor parcels show active lots at this location without street addresses (for example lot 3941041, added 2019-02-07), so whether the park has its own Assessor lot was not established from a cited source; this feature uses the OSM boundary instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Delivered under the Port of San Francisco's Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (2010) as the public-open-space component of the Pier 70 area (Port Item 12B, Sept 2018: identified in the 2010 Preferred Master Plan; HPC 2013 packet: a separate project), distinct from and adjacent to Brookfield's 28-acre D4D redevelopment parcel from which Pier & Point's other Pier 70 shapes are drawn. Built around a stabilized historic gantry crane and the historic Slipway 4 (Port Resolution 18-61 lists 'stabilization of historic gantry crane (non-functional)'; the crane cabs were eliminated); a human-powered boating center was listed only as a future development opportunity, and Dogpatch Paddle rentals operate from the adjacent YMCA building (Port park page).

records.name: Building 12 Plaza and Market Square
records.summary: The roughly 1.5-acre 'social centerpiece' of the Pier 70 open-space network (D4D Section 3.9): Market Square between Buildings 2 and 12 and Parcel D, the Building 12 entry plaza on 22nd Street, a Maryland Street platform for vendors and food trucks, and possibly the retained structural frame of Building 15. Building 12 itself reopened in 2022 and Maryland Street's paving is done, but the plaza is a Phase 1 park still tied to adjacent vertical development.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- derived from a real, street-polygonized city block (not a diagram pixel-trace), subtracting Building 2, Parcel D, and Building 12's own mapped shapes. This is a deliberate departure from pure diagram-tracing: since Figure 6.4.2's own green fill didn't precisely reach the real (satellite-corrected) edges of Building 2 and Building 12, using the real block boundary instead better matches both the drawing's evident intent (this block reads as fully built-out, buildings plus plaza, no gaps) and the satellite ground truth. The block polygon's north edge stops slightly short of Parcel D's own north edge (~14m, since the not-yet-built '21st St (NEW)' isn't in real street data) -- unioned with D's own extent to avoid an artificial gap there. Area (~1.38 acres) is close to, but still a bit under, the D4D's cited ~1.5 acres for this named space -- the cause of the gap is not established: the D4D (Section 3.9) also counts a Maryland Street Platform along Maryland St as part of the space and places the Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd St, so the plaza's extent here may differ from the D4D's in more than one way (the dashed '15' box on the diagram is the legend's approximate location of the mid-block passage beside Building 15, not a boundary of this space).
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155); named per Figure 3.4.1 - Overview of Public Spaces (p.52), zone 5.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own identified: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that the site is unaddressed and not subdivided is withdrawn; whether the plaza's block has its own lot has not been checked against the recorded final map.
notes.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3.9), approximately 1.5 acres. Per Section 3.9, Market Square lies north of Building 12 (between Building 2 and Parcel D, entered from 21st St), the Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd St, and the Maryland Street Platform along Building 12's Maryland St side; the mapped block spans Louisiana St to Maryland St.

facts.value: 3.9 'Building 12 Plaza and Market Square', zone 5 of Figure 3.4.1
approximately 1.5 (D4D Section 3.4)

Market Square (flanked by rehabilitated buildings and new construction on three sides, four access ways, a compact tree grove), Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd Street, Maryland Street Platform, and the Building 15 structural frame pending a structural feasibility study
A pedestrian opening on 21st Street between Building 2 and Parcel D; the existing passageway through Buildings 2 and 12; a Building 12 entrance from 22nd Street; a direct entry from Maryland Street
Open-air markets, community gatherings, small performances; Market Square extends Maryland Street with coordinated paving to accommodate vendors and food trucks

Within the Phase 1 area (Port's 2026 Exhibit A); Port Item 9B (2017, Table A) lists Building 12 Plaza (OS-1) and Market Square (OS-2) among the Phase 1 parks, and Port Item 11A cites three acres of Phase 1 parks overall

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel K South (PKS)
records.summary: The southern piece of the Port's 20th/Illinois Street parcel, on Illinois Street south of the new 21st Street, reserved under the 2017 approvals as a 100%-affordable housing site (65 ft under the D4D). The Port's 2026 report assigns it to Phase 2 and says its gap funding is not yet available; no developer has been selected.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward). It is Parcel K South, a Port-retained parcel created from the Port's Illinois & 20th Street Parcel (Port Item 9B, Res 17-52), outside the 28-Acre Site and the developer's vertical option, so it is not within Brookfield's 28-acre district. It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the surrounding Pier 70 land re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address), and Port Item 9B gives the Illinois & 20th Street Parcel as Block 4110 Lot 001 (DataSF lists 4110001 as retired 2018-10-02). RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (how the shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. This deliberately does NOT match today's satellite imagery of the parking lot -- this parcel's boundary represents the D4D's planned footprint, including '21ST ST (NEW)', which is not built yet.

notes.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. PKS is part of the Port's Illinois & 20th Street Parcel (Assessor's Block 4110/Lot 001 per Port Item 9B), which Resolution 17-52 has the Port subdivide into four parcels; it is outside Brookfield's 28-acre site, so the earlier statement that it is part of that site is withdrawn. DataSF lists 4110001 as retired (2018-10-02); which current lot corresponds to PKS has not been checked, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential in every D4D land-use scenario (Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7), 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2, and a 100%-affordable housing site under Port Item 9B. records.name: Pier 70 Hoedown Yard 3 (HDY3)
records.summary: The northern parcel of the PG&E-owned Hoedown Yard at Illinois and 22nd Streets, zoned residential under the Pier 70 SUD and D4D (65 ft) but not part of Brookfield's 28-Acre Project: the City holds an option to buy the roughly 3-acre yard from PG&E, subdivide it into three parcels and offer them for sale, with an Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District over the yard meant to fund Pier 70's affordable housing. No sale, developer or construction has been recorded.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward). It is part of the Hoedown Yard, which the D4D (Section 1) describes as owned by Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E), with a City option to acquire it, and which is outside Brookfield's 28-Acre Site. The D4D gives the yard's Assessor lots as Block 4120 Lot 002 and Block 4110 Lot 008A (Port Item 9B gives 4120/002 and 4711/008A); DataSF's Assessor layer lists 4120002 and 4110008A (1021 Illinois St) as active lots, and this hand-traced block overlaps them, but the overlay of approximate geometry is not an identification of this block's own lot. RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. SNAPPED 2026-09-17: this block's north edge had drifted 1.26m south of PKS's own south edge (both blocks were independently re-measured at different times and no longer shared an exact boundary, despite the diagram showing them as one continuous fill with only an internal divider line). Snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's south-edge coordinates exactly, closing the gap to 0m. RE-SNAPPED 2026-09-17 (same day): PKS itself was found to be badly mispositioned (60% of its area was being clipped away against the real 21st St -- see the Parcel K South (PKS) record) and was shifted ~25m south to ground-truth against the real street. Re-snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's new south edge to stay attached; area dropped from ~2,699 to ~1,508 sq m as a direct, expected consequence of PKS moving into what was previously this block's own north portion. This block's own south/diagonal portion (touching HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground) is unchanged. INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (after this block was noted to look too small relative to its peers in the drawing): checked whether this shrinkage is a real bug (i.e., whether the same northward transform bias found on PKS/C1/PKN/Building 113-116 also affects this block's own south/diagonal portion, which would justify shifting HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground south too, restoring this block's diagram-implied size while keeping everything attached). Tested this directly: interpolated the real, official 22nd St centerline's latitude at HDY1/2's own south-edge longitudes (the nearest independently-checkable real street to this cluster) and compared to HDY1/2's current south edge -- found a clean ~14m gap with NO overlap, unlike PKS's 60% real-street overlap that justified its own correction. This is the opposite signature from a 'drawn too far north' bug: if the same bias reached this far south, HDY1/2 would itself be overlapping 22nd St, not comfortably clear of it. Conclusion: the 21st-St-row bias is local to that row and does not extend to this block's own south portion or to HDY1/2/Irish Hill Playground -- there is no evidence basis to shift them south to recover this block's pre-fix size. This block's current, smaller size is treated as the accurate, forced consequence of ground-truthing PKS (which shares this block's own north edge), not an unresolved bug. This conclusion is stated explicitly because Pier & Point does not fabricate geometry: if a future source shows this block's own south/diagonal corners were independently misread (a diagram-reading error, not a bias-correction consequence), that would still warrant revisiting this specific block on its own.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcel layer shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address) and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008, so which lot, if any, corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free fit of the plan drawing to the map -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects that fit's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. RESOLVED 2026-09-16: no longer overlaps 'Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)' -- that building's placement was corrected to its real position elsewhere on the site. CORRECTED 2026-09-17: this block was found to carry the same image-scale error in tracing already found on Parcel K North, Parcel K South and Hoedown Yard 3. Its true south edge sits ~26m further north than previously recorded, which had been silently eating into Irish Hill Playground's real extent. CLIPPED 2026-09-17 against the real, rehabilitated Building 113-116 footprint (not a planned-demolition overlap). Each of these changes is logged in this shape's data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).

notes.regulatory_context: Flexible use: the D4D's Figure 2.1.1 stripes C1 Commercial-Office, Residential and Parking Garage, and its land-use scenarios show a garage or partial garage, 'permitted to be residential or commercial based on future parking needs' (use set to 'mixed' on the map); 90 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (a uniform height, not a 65-90 ft range). open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.
The C2A affordable project's unit count beyond 'at least 100', its cost and its financing are all listed as TBD by the developer; no MOHCD loan approval or Port ground lease for C2A was found.

The 2017 approvals counted 320+ stand-alone affordable units across three sites (C1B, C2A, Parcel K South); the 2026 report holds the minimum at 327 and says the parties are evaluating higher unit yields, but no per-site split was published.

The developer page cited for C2A (Chinatown CDC's 'In Development' list) does not name Parcel C2A; that the 'Pier 70' entry is the C2A project is inferred from the Port's Aug 2026 report naming the same developers for Parcel C2A. A Port or MOHCD document naming C2A and the unit count would settle it.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel D
records.summary: Phase 1 residential parcel between Building 2 and the new 21st Street, 90 ft under the D4D, designed by Stanley Saitowitz | Natoma Architects as an L-shaped building of seven residential levels over ground-floor retail with loft townhouses along 21st Street. It has not started construction; the Port's proposed 2026 amendments would require closing on it by 2029-2030.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address) and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008, so which lot, if any, corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free fit of the plan figure to the map -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this fit's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential (studio-3BR over 7 levels) + ground-floor retail + townhouses along 21st St, designed by Stanley Saitowitz/Natoma Architects, per the architect's own project page (saitowitz.com/pier-70-parcel-d): 'loft town houses along 21st street. Above are studio, one, two and three bedroom units stacked on seven levels', with a retail space along the grove, Market Square and Maryland Street. A weak secondary source implied a ~2020 completion, which no primary source supports: Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward and that no Phase 1 option parcel has been exercised. The Real Deal (Jul 16, 2026) reports Brookfield's development VP saying additional density would let the company 'break ground in 2027 on its first market-rate apartment building' (350 units, parcel not named), a conditional plan not specific to Parcel D. Treat as NOT yet built.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the Port's Item 11A staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026, for the Aug 11, 2026 meeting), which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Unit count, square footage and the date of the Saitowitz design are not stated on the architect's page and no Planning vertical design approval for Parcel D is listed on the Planning Department's Pier 70 page.
A secondary source implying a ~2020 completion is noted on this parcel's map shape; no primary source supports it, and Port Item 11A says Phase 1 vertical construction has not moved forward.

records.summary: Residential parcel on Maryland Street north of Building 21, mostly 90 ft with a 65 ft north leg under the D4D, assigned to Phase 2C in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. Under the 2017 DDA the lease of historic Building 21 is triggered within a year after completion of the building on E1.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address) and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008, so which lot, if any, corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential, mostly 90 ft max with a smaller 65 ft strip along its north leg per Figure 6.4.2. No construction-start source found. Geometry here is a simplified bounding shape -- the real parcel has an irregular footprint around the historic Building 21 (mapped separately in this project) immediately to its southeast.

The SF YIMBY summary describing E-1A/E-1B as ~120,000 gsf of retail and arts space conflicts with the D4D's residential designation for E1; the underlying filing was not retrieved, so this is left as reported.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel E2 (block)
records.summary: Phase 1 rental-apartment parcel at 185 Maryland Street (Block 4116 Lot 008), 50,875 sq ft, entitled for about 280 units with 20% below-market-rate, with a 2021 SF YIMBY post crediting its design to Kennerly Architecture and Planning. Its 2020 appraisal ($5 million against an $11.3 million DDA threshold) and a second below-threshold appraisal in 2021 triggered the down-market delay that has stalled Phase 1; the Port's proposed 2026 amendments make it the first parcel the developer must take down.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Parcel E2 is not yet built (Port Item 11A, memo dated Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward, and no Phase 1 option parcel has been exercised) and it does have its own Assessor lot: Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Assessor's Block 4116, Lot 008 (185 Maryland Street), and DataSF's Assessor layer lists 4116008 as an active P70-MU lot added 2019-02-07 with no street address. This record still uses hand-traced approximate geometry from the D4D diagram; whether to replace it with the real lot has not been decided (Pier 70's map shapes are signed off as they stand). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free fit of the plan figure to the map (how this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this fit's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17: this block's south edge fell well short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery -- 13m short at the SW corner, 25m short at the SE corner (a growing gap toward the east, consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the Illinois/Michigan St reference points used to fit the plan figure to the map). Extended each south vertex independently by its own measured gap (rather than a uniform shift) so the block's south edge now reaches the real sidewalk across its full width, matching Figure 6.4.2's own convention of drawing blocks flush to the street.

notes.regulatory_context: Shown at 70 ft max per Figure 6.4.2, the same height tier as Parcel E3. The Port's sources treat this as the one Parcel E2: Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) describes E2 (185 Maryland Street) as a residential parcel entitled for approximately 280 rental dwelling units, and Port Item 9B (2017, Table A) ties Slipways Commons (SC-1) to one year after the TCO for Parcel E2; no source found describes a second 'E2', so the earlier 'possible labeling inconsistency' flag is withdrawn. No construction-start source found for this block.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel E3
names: Elevation Sky Park San Francisco (interim use)
records.summary: Waterfront residential parcel at 22nd Street and the Bay, 70 ft under the D4D and assigned to Phase 3A in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. Its D4D building has no construction record; instead Elevation XR, with Brookfield, is developing the interim Elevation Sky Park entertainment venue (three projection domes and a pyramid on about 165,000 sq ft, a five-year term) on 'Phase 2/3 sites' here; a one-day festival, Pier Play San Francisco, was held on the site on September 19, 2026, and the venue's own page calls it 'the future home of Elevation Sky Park', with no opening date yet.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block's boundary is a hand-traced D4D diagram parcel, not a surveyed lot; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade (the transform's validation is recorded in this shape's mapping log in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17: this block's south edge fell ~22m short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery, part of the same local scale error documented on Parcel A/E2 (parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors land short of their true extent). Extended both south vertices by 22m to reach the sidewalk. Note this is still the D4D diagram's original 'E3' boundary, not a re-survey of ESP's own real tent/dome footprint -- see the ESP-merge note below for that separate uncertainty. CURRENT USE, POST-LEASE FUTURE UNCLEAR (added 2026-09-17): this parcel is being treated as the site of Elevation Sky Park, a real interim entertainment venue confirmed to be under a 5-year lease (see the regulatory context) -- that part is sourced fact. What is NOT known, and should not be assumed, is what happens here after that lease ends: the D4D's original masterplan designates this parcel 70ft-max residential, but that plan was adopted years before ESP's interim lease existed, and no source found ties ESP's lease expiration to an actual scheduled residential construction start, or confirms the D4D's original boundary/use for this specific parcel will still be pursued unchanged by then. Do not read the 'entertainment' use here as a permanent reclassification, or assume 'residential' will automatically resume -- both are open questions. The parcel-level match to ESP itself is also still an approximation: no scaled site plan for the venue was found (an earlier note cited a rendering in an SFGATE article, but no article link was recorded, so that corroboration is not relied on), and ESP's real footprint may still extend slightly into neighboring E2/E4, as the pre-merge overlap analysis found.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No source read ties this parcel to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor parcels include lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019 (Port Item 12B, Feb 2020, gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116, Lot 008), and an active lot 4116009 with no street address lies at about this location next to E2's lot, but no source read confirms it as E3's; this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: D4D-designated use: residential, 70 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (no construction-start source ever found for that plan). CURRENT REAL USE: Elevation Sky Park (Elevation XR, in partnership with Brookfield Properties), a 165,000 sq ft interim entertainment venue (3 geodesic domes + a pyramid) under a 5-year lease, to be fully permitted through the Port of San Francisco (community engagement deck, June 2025, future tense). A one-day festival, RASA World's 'Pier Play San Francisco', was held on the site on September 19, 2026; the venue's own page (Sept 2026) calls the site 'the future home of Elevation Sky Park' and invites sign-ups for opening announcements, and the July 2026 release had said the campus would open in phases beginning September 2026. No source shows the venue open. Port materials describe it as an 'interim activation on Phase 2/3 sites within Pier 70 development zone' -- confirming it is temporary by design, though not tied to a specific successor project or date.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Placement of Elevation Sky Park on Parcel E3 is Pier & Point's own reading (Pier & Point merged it into E3, per this record's mapping log): the primary sources say only 'Phase 2/3 sites' and 'where 22nd Street meets the Bay', which is consistent with E3/H2 but not parcel-specific. A Port license or permit for the venue, which would settle it, was not found on any 2025-2026 Port Commission agenda.

Pier Play San Francisco, the venue's first public event, was held on Sept 19, 2026 per the venue's own page (published Sept 25, 2026), which calls the site 'the future home of Elevation Sky Park'; whether the venue is open on a continuing basis is not stated by any source read. The Business Wire release itself could not be checked; a syndicated copy on Yahoo Finance was read.
Lease or license terms (rent to Brookfield or the Port) for the interim venue: not found.

When Elevation Sky Park itself opens (as a venue, not the Sept 19, 2026 one-day festival): its own page (checked 2026-09-29) still calls the site its future home and offers opening-announcement sign-ups.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel E4
records.summary: The waterfront arts-building parcel east of Building 21: excluded from the developer's purchase option, capped at 50 ft and five stories, and reserved under the 2017 DDA for a roughly 90,000 sq ft arts facility (with replacement studios for the Noonan Building artists) on a 50-year, $1-a-year lease once $17.5 million in private contributions is raised. The Port's proposed 2026 amendments would rezone it to allow housing if the arts facility proves infeasible.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel; E4 is in any case excluded from the developer's option). The block has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address); this hand-traced block overlaps mostly active lot 4052011 (about 77%) and 4052010 (about 15%) in that layer, which is only an overlay of approximate geometry, not an identification, and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008. No source read describes the block's current ground condition. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see the mapping log) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. E4 lies within the 28-Acre Site, whose developer is Brookfield's affiliate FC Pier 70, LLC (Port Items 9B and 12B), and DataSF's Assessor layer shows most of the site's re-mapped lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07) with no street address. The earlier statement that the site has not been subdivided per the masterplan's named parcels is withdrawn (named parcels have lots: Port Item 12B gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008); this block's own lot has not been identified, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's land-use designation for E4 is Retail, Arts and Light Industrial (Figure 2.1.1), with office uses permitted in Building 12 and E4 except on the ground floor, and residential not permitted on E4 (Table 2.1.1) -- not residential or general mixed-use as sometimes described secondhand. Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) calls it 'the arts building parcel (Parcel E4)' and lists it among the parcels excluded from the developer's standard option under the DDA. Recorded here as 'mixed' only because this map has no dedicated 'arts' use category. Max height 50 ft per Figure 6.4.2 -- the lowest of any parcel at Pier 70. Port Item 11A (2026) proposes to allow residential use on E4 if an arts facility proves infeasible. No construction-start source found.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the Port's Item 11A staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026, for the Aug 11, 2026 meeting), which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.
Brookfield's leasing brochure reportedly gives '+/- 410,000 RSF' for F-G; the brochure was not retrievable, so the figure is neither restated here nor kept in the geometry file.

The parcel's south edge abuts the former Potrero Power Station site; no Port document retrieved describes coordination of F/G with that project beyond the shared pump-station framework mentioned in the June 2025 deck.

records.summary: Flexible commercial-office/residential parcel (baseline scenario residential) on the south side of 22nd Street east of Maryland Street (west half of the H1/H2 pair), 90 ft under the D4D (six stories for commercial buildings, nine for residential), assigned to Phase 3A with Parcel E3 in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'), and no source read ties it to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcels include new lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019, without street addresses, but which lot (if any) is this block's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free fit of the plan drawing to the map -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects that fit's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data. Each of these changes is logged in this shape's data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No source read ties this block to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor parcels include lots created for Brookfield's 28-acre district in 2019 (for example, Port Item 12B, Feb 2020, gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116, Lot 008), but this block's own lot was not identified, so this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Flexible commercial-office/residential parcel: D4D Figure 2.1.1 stripes H1 as Commercial-Office and Residential; the baseline (Mid-Point) and Maximum Residential scenarios show it residential and only the Maximum Office scenario shows it commercial. 90 ft max per Figure 6.4.2; six stories for commercial buildings and nine for residential (D4D Section 6.4.2). An earlier note citing Brookfield's leasing brochure (pure office use; a combined ~430,000 RSF for H1-H2) was removed 2026-09-29 because the brochure is not cited or retrieved. No construction-start source found.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Brookfield's leasing brochure reportedly gives a combined '+/- 430,000 RSF' for H1-H2 and calls H1 pure office; the brochure was not retrieved, so those statements were removed from the geometry file on 2026-09-29.
Whether the Elevation Sky Park interim venue extends onto H2 (the Port described it as 'where 22nd Street meets the Bay' on 'Phase 2/3 sites'): unresolved; see the Parcel E3 record.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel H2
records.summary: Flexible commercial-office/residential parcel (baseline scenario residential) on the south side of 22nd Street east of Maryland Street (east half of the H1/H2 pair), 90 ft under the D4D (six stories for commercial buildings, nine for residential), assigned to Phase 3A with Parcel E3 in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. No design, appraisal or construction record exists for it.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'), and no source read ties it to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcels include new lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019, without street addresses, but which lot (if any) is this block's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No source read ties this block to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor parcels include lots created for Brookfield's 28-acre district in 2019 (for example, Port Item 12B, Feb 2020, gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116, Lot 008), but this block's own lot was not identified, so this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Flexible commercial-office/residential parcel: D4D Figure 1.5.5 (baseline) shows H2 residential and only the Maximum Office scenario shows it commercial; 90 ft max per Figure 6.4.2; six stories for commercial buildings and nine for residential (D4D Section 6.4.2). An earlier note of the same ~430,000 RSF program as Parcel H1 was removed 2026-09-29 (no source read gives an RSF figure for H1/H2). No construction-start source found.

facts.value: FC Pier 70, LLC, an affiliate of Brookfield Properties (originally Forest City)
Port of San Francisco (Seawall Lot 349; option parcels are ground-leased for 99 years except condominium parcels, which may be sold)
SITELAB urban studio (lead author); Grimshaw Architecture (commercial), David Baker Architects (residential), James Corner Field Operations (landscape)

Flexible commercial-office/residential parcel: D4D Figure 2.1.1 stripes H2 as Commercial-Office and Residential; the Mid-Point (baseline) and Maximum Residential scenarios (Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7) show H1 and H2 residential, and only the Maximum Office scenario shows them commercial (and labels them 'H1/H2')
90 (D4D Figure 6.4.2)
6 stories for commercial buildings, 9 for residential (D4D S6.4.2)
Phase 3A with E3 (Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan, Exhibit A)
75% of the 22nd Street frontage (D4D S2.2.5)

Waterfront Promenade outdoor dining terraces may be located adjacent to the east face of H2; the 22nd Street viewing pavilion extends 22nd Street to the Bay, and a tree grove runs parallel to the Bay Trail at the southern edge of the site (D4D Section 3.7)

records.name: Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)
records.summary: A six-story board-formed concrete warehouse of 1941-44 (256 ft by 77 ft, 98,804 sq ft) north of Building 12, one of the historic buildings addressed in the Pier 70 DDA; unlike Buildings 12 and 21, it is an option parcel that must be developed under a 99-year lease consistent with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards if the developer exercises its option. It is a Phase 1 option parcel to be held on a 99-year lease at an appraised rent; a 2021 filing described about 120 apartments in its shell, Brookfield now markets it as creative office, and the Port's proposed 2026 amendments would have the developer assign its option and close escrow within six months of Board approval, with certain impact fees and special taxes waived. No rehabilitation has started.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- RELOCATED 2026-09-16 from an incorrect west-lot placement (logged, with the rest of this shape's history, in its data file in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record) to Figure 6.4.2's own labeled '2' Historic Building box, in the same east-side node as Buildings 12 and 21. Traced automatically from the figure's legend color, not hand-verified vertex-by-vertex; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, consistent with this site's other diagram-traced parcels. The close match (85%) between this trace's area and Warehouse No. 2's documented 236ft x 76ft footprint is a good independent sanity check, but this is still a simplified rectangle, not a surveyed building outline.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Officially 'Warehouse No. 2' per the D4D (Section 6.6.1), a historic industrial shop structure, footprint 236 ft x 76 ft. Its use is not settled: the D4D treats it as a flexible parcel (Figure 2.1.1 stripes it Commercial-Office/Residential; the land-use scenarios in Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7 show it Residential in the Mid-Point baseline and Maximum Residential and Commercial-Office in Maximum Office), a 2021 development-agreement filing summarised about 120 dwelling units (SF YIMBY), and Brookfield's leasing page (pier70sf.com/leasing) shows 'creative office'. The NRHP gross area is 98,804 sq ft; a ~100,000 RSF brochure figure and a '~50,000 GSF, Arts/Maker' description formerly recorded here are uncited and have been dropped. No source found confirms whether rehabilitation has started; absent from the Port's own June 2025 progress update.

records.summary: The 1917 Classical Revival main office of the Union Iron Works at the corner of 20th and Illinois Streets, designed by Frederick H. Meyer, rehabilitated by Orton Development under the Port's 66-year Historic Core master lease and subleased whole to RH (Restoration Hardware) on a 41-year sublease from February 2017; RH San Francisco, with the Palm Court restaurant and a rooftop park, opened May 13, 2022.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) -- high confidence in the outline itself. The match to 'Building 101' specifically (as opposed to a neighboring structure) rests on position (33.9m from the diagram's own label, closest of any candidate) and shape correspondence, not an address or explicit building-number tag in the footprint dataset itself, since no such attribute exists there.

notes.why_no_real_parcel: The HPC packet of Nov 2013 places the building on Assessor's Block 4046, Lot 001 (blklot 4046001), but DataSF shows that lot retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn); the building's footprint now lies within active lot 3941027, which has no street address in DataSF's Assessor parcels. This feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: Bethlehem Steel HQ, a 1917 neoclassical office building designed by Frederick H. Meyer, ~80,000 sf, 5 floors plus 2 lower levels and a penthouse. Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) starting after a Nov 26 2013 Historic Preservation Commission review (sfplanning.org HPC packet 2013.1168E); per that packet, the seismic upgrade uses shear walls, and the rehab preserves the historic exterior elevations while adapting the interior. The Port's Jan 2019 update reported Buildings 101 and 102 still under construction, with completion and occupancy of Building 101 anticipated in 2020. RH San Francisco -- 'The Gallery at the Historic Bethlehem Steel Building' (showroom, Palm Court restaurant and two wine bars, rooftop park) opened May 13, 2022.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 102 (former Power House)
records.summary: The 1912 Classical Revival powerhouse on 20th Street between Buildings 101 and 104, designed by Charles Peter Weeks, which generated compressed air and distributed electricity for the shipyard and still housed BAE Systems' electrical service when rehabilitation began. Orton rebuilt it as office space with a mezzanine and a rear addition (about 15,300-18,000 sq ft) and subleased it to JUUL Labs for ten years; the current occupant is unknown.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself. CORRECTED 2026-09-29: this footprint's area (~1955 m2 / ~21,043 sqft) does not match the building. The National Register nomination gives Building 102's dimensions as 128 ft 6 in by 42 ft 4 in (about 5,440 sqft, ~505 m2 as a rectangle), so this outline is roughly four times the building's own footprint and probably includes neighboring structures or other area; the '11,266 sf' Port figure is not the likely source of the discrepancy. The geometry has been accepted as is and was not changed; the outline should not be read as the building's own footprint.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The former Assessor lot blklot 4046001 (which held Buildings 101, 102, 104 and 122/123 in the 2013 HPC packet) was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, active=false); in DataSF's current layer this footprint falls within active lot 3941041, which has no street address. No cited source ties the building to a current lot, so this feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: The former Power House, built 1912, part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as Building 101 (HPC packet 2013.1168E, Nov 26 2013 review). Per that packet, Building 102 was 'in fairly good condition' at the time and in use as the powerhouse facility. Port Item 12A (memo dated Jan 4, 2019) names JUUL Labs as the ten-year sublessee of the entire building less the Port's basement electrical equipment room, and Potrero View (Mar 2019) says JUUL 'sublets offices in Building 102'; no source after 2020 confirms a current occupant.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters)
records.summary: The 1896 red-brick Renaissance Revival office of the Union Iron Works on 20th Street, by Percy & Hamilton, the earliest of the architect-designed buildings along that street (NRHP); red-tagged when Orton took it on, with new steel columns proposed for seismic bracing in the 2013 plan, and back in occupancy with a certificate of occupancy in June 2017. It was subleased to Tea Living (Tea Collection); the Port's 2019 table lists JUUL Labs, under sublease from Tea Living, for the entire building on a ten-year term from June 2017.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 104. Buildings 122 and 123 (two small one-story 'check house' buildings flanking Building 104, per the 2013 HPC packet -- 774 GSF and 400 GSF respectively) are NOT separately represented here or anywhere else in this dataset: no footprint of a matching small size was found immediately adjacent to this one, most likely because DataSF's building-footprint extraction merged them into this building's outline (or Building 102's) given how small and closely attached they are. Their combined ~1,174 GSF (~109 m2) is a small fraction of this footprint's ~1,080 m2 total, so if merged in, they would not meaningfully distort this shape -- but their own individual positions are not confirmed and are not claimed here.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The HPC packet of Nov 2013 places the building on Assessor's Block 4046, Lot 001 (blklot 4046001), but DataSF shows that lot retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn); the building's footprint now lies within active lot 3941027, which has no street address in DataSF's Assessor parcels. This feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: UIW (Union Iron Works) Headquarters, Building 104, a Renaissance Revival structure built in 1896 with a distinctive clerestory top floor, unreinforced masonry construction. Per the 2013 HPC packet (2013.1168E), it was previously used as a naval hospital/medical office (WWII-era conversion) and was a 'red-tagged,' seismically challenged building at review time; rehab included demolishing demising walls from the WWII conversion. Part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. as Buildings 101/102. The Port's Jan 2019 update gives 45,237 sq ft (the NRHP nomination gives 37,641) and reports a Certificate of Occupancy in June 2017. Named occupants in the sources read: Tea Living (Tea Collection) as sublessee and JUUL Labs as its subtenant from June 2017 (Port Item 12A, Jan 2019; Potrero View, June 2018); no current tenant is confirmed.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop)
names: Union Iron Works Foundry and Warehouse
records.summary: The oldest surviving shipyard buildings at Pier 70: the 1885-86 brick Machine Shop and blacksmith/boiler shop (113/114, joined by a 1914 concrete connector, 492 ft long) and the 1916-17 reinforced-concrete foundry and warehouse (115/116) beside it. Closed and red-tagged in 2001, they were rehabilitated by Orton Development with a buckling-restrained-brace steel system and public atrium, receiving certificates of occupancy in November 2017 (115/116) and April 2018 (113/114), and were subleased to Uber Advanced Technologies Group and Gusto.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprints -- high confidence in each piece's outline and in the group's overall position (confirmed to sit within Figure 6.4.2's own '113-116' box). Individual identification of which piece(s) correspond to Building 113 vs 114 vs 115 vs 116 specifically is NOT possible from the sources checked -- Figure 6.4.2 draws them as one undifferentiated box, and the 2013 HPC packet's textual description ('115 and 116 abut Building 113/114') does not give a precise position. Rather than guess, this feature represents the combined complex, consistent with how it is actually shown in the source diagram. The combined footprint here (~9751 sq m / ~104,957 sqft) is larger than Building 113/114 alone (~86,100 sqft per its documented 492ft x 175ft footprint) and smaller than 113/114 + 115/116's combined documented GSF (~95,000 + ~38,000 = ~133,000 GSF) -- broadly consistent given GSF can include multi-level floor area not captured by a footprint, but not independently verified piece-by-piece.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The former Assessor lot blklot 4111004, which held these buildings, has no street address and was retired by DataSF on 2018-10-02 (active=false). Block 4111 now has active P70-MU lots 4111005-4111010 (added 2019-02-07) and this footprint falls within active lot 4111008, also with no street address; no source cited here ties a current lot to Buildings 113-116. This feature uses the real building footprints instead, matched to the specific area that Figure 6.4.2 itself draws as the historic '113-116' complex.
notes.regulatory_context: Union Iron Works Machine Shop and Foundry, Buildings 113/114, on the south side of 20th Street just east of Illinois Street -- 'one of the most valuable and most vulnerable historic resources on the site' per the 2013 HPC packet (2013.1168E). Two unreinforced brick structures (built in 1885 and 1886 per the HPC packet; the National Register nomination says the eastern, 1885 portion housed the blacksmith and boiler shop and the western, 1886 portion the machine shop) joined in 1914 by a reinforced concrete connector; building-length skylights, rows of high arched windows; ~95,000 GSF, 492ft long by 175ft wide, ~62ft tall. Buildings 115 and 116 abut Building 113/114, constructed 1916-1917, ~38,000 GSF, 57ft tall, with 'unusual windows and monitor skylights.' At review time the complex was red-tagged and subject to an engineer's advisory of imminent collapse. Rehab by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) was proposed (HPC packet) to include 'abatement, demolition or relocation of metal additions to the building on the western and southern facades', a new steel seismic system tied into the brick perimeter, and demolition of two minor eastern appendages (Buildings 23/24, ~1,500 GSF). Proposed for industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail, alongside Building 14, framing a shared ~45,000 sf courtyard.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 14
records.summary: A World War II double-gable corrugated-metal heavy warehouse east of the Machine Shop, framing, with Buildings 113-116, a ~45,000 sq ft courtyard per the 2013 planning packet (the National Register nomination has it forming a courtyard with Building 2); one of the smaller of Orton's Historic Core buildings at 16,315 sq ft before rehabilitation (Port's 2019 memo), rehabilitated with a new mezzanine and seismic bracing (certificate of occupancy August 2017) and subleased whole to Obscura Digital (The Madison Square Garden Company) for seven years from September 2017.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 14: position matches Figure 6.4.2's own label (39m away, the closest and only plausible candidate among the lot's other footprint pieces once 113/114/115/116's own pieces are excluded) and its area independently matches the previously-cited 16,315 GSF within 3%. As with the other buildings Pier & Point has split from oversized Assessor lots, the match rests on position and size, not an explicit building-number attribute in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll and no distinct Assessor lot of its own. Its footprint lay about 76% on the former lot blklot 4052001 and about 24% on former lot 4111003, both retired by DataSF on 2018-10-02; it now falls within active lot 4111008 (no street address, shared with Buildings 113-116). The 2013 HPC packet lists Block 4046 Lot 001, Block 4111 Lots 003 and 004 and a portion of Block 4052 Lot 001 as the project location for the ten historic buildings; the earlier statement that Buildings 101/102/104/113-116/21 shared one lot with Building 14 is withdrawn (101/102/104 lay on 4046001 and 113-116 on 4111004). This feature uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: Building 14, a basic heavy warehouse dated to 1941 (per the 2013 HPC packet, 2013.1168E) with approximately 16,000 GSF of space and a 66 foot height, sits immediately east of the Union Iron Works Machine Shop complex (Buildings 113/114/115/116), framing, with them, an approximately 45,000 square foot courtyard per the 2013 HPC packet's rehabilitation concept (not the D4D). Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as part of the same 20th Street Historic Core project; proposed for the same industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail as its neighbors.

records.name: Potrero Power Station Block 1
records.summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan with a stepped height envelope up to 180 ft, one of three blocks (with 5 and 13) eligible to host the project's single permitted district parking garage; no design review approval or construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram by fitting it to multiple real street points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 with control-point georeferencing. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third revision) in a single consistent measurement across the whole block layout. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth revision) after a mis-measured control point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). The statement that the block is unbuilt, on vacant/graded land and unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll is our own observation (satellite imagery and the Assessor roll), not something the cited 2020 D4D can show; the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) does not list a Block 1 application. The statement that the diagram is dated 2020 is confirmed by the final D4D's footer (February 26, 2020).
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. (This is our own reading of the parcel data, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The 2018 draft EIR (Vol. 1, PDF p.107) says a portion of Block 1 lies within the PG&E sub-area, which is part of Assessor's Block 4175/Lot 018, so an unsubdivided Assessor lot does underlie part of this block.
notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (printed p.245) shows Block 1, marked '1*' (a potential district parking garage location up to 90 ft in height and potential grocery store location), in two height zones read from the figure's colour-coded labels: '180'/85'' on its west part (maximum height 180 ft, maximum base height 85 ft) and '85'' on its east part. The '115'MAX' marking on the figure is a plan-dimension line for the tower zone, not a height. notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, fitted to real street positions at multiple points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. The shape was rebuilt on 2026-09-16 with a more careful fit of the diagram to the map, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and corrected again that day after one mis-measured reference point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). CLIPPED 2026-09-17: although this record's regulatory notes already said the shape was 'clipped to exclude Sophie Maxwell's real footprint,' a fresh check of overlaps between real parcels and approximate shapes found this polygon still overlapped Sophie Maxwell (block/lot 4232020) by 1,082 sq m -- the clip described in that text was apparently never actually applied to (or was lost from) the published shape. It was then re-clipped against block/lot 4232020's real parcel boundary; area dropped from ~4,965 to ~3,883 sq m. This overlap had gone undetected because Pier & Point's automated shape check only compared approximate shapes with each other, never with real parcels. The vacant/graded and unaddressed-in-the-Assessor-roll wording is our own observation, not something the cited 2020 D4D can show; 'not yet built' is consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which says the developer had submitted no building permits for any market-rate housing projects. The 2020 date of the diagram is confirmed by the final D4D's footer (February 26, 2020). DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) lists active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 after the Phase 1 Final Map, most unaddressed; whether one of them corresponds to this block was not checked, so the statement that no subdivided Assessor parcel exists for it is unverified.

notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (printed p.245) shows Block 7 as one numbered block, with its height zones read from the figure's colour-coded labels: the north-west part (on Humboldt St at Louisiana Paseo) is labelled 240'/85' (maximum height 240 ft, maximum base height 85 ft) and the rest of the block (east side and south strip) is 85'; the two '150'MAX' markings are plan dimensions of the tower, not heights. The D4D numbers only 'Block 7'; 'Block 7A' and 'Block 7B' are the names SF Planning's own approvals use for the two buildings (e.g. 'Approval of the Design Review Application of Block 7A', March 2, 2022, Case 2017-011878PHA-04, and Block 7B, March 2, 2022). The Sophie Maxwell Building ('Block 7b, the Sophie Maxwell Building' in the 2024 annual compliance report; real blklot 4232020, addressed 1212 MARYLAND in DataSF Parcels; already mapped separately in this dataset) occupies part of this block; this polygon is the REMAINING portion, clipped to exclude Sophie Maxwell's real footprint (the clipping is our own work). The remainder is presumed to correspond to 'Block 7A' (Foster + Partners-designed rental tower, press-reported heights of 240-264 ft depending on source, consistent with this figure's 240 ft max) -- design review approved March 2, 2022; the 2024 annual compliance report says no market-rate building permits had been submitted; no construction-start source found.
