open_questions: Construction start: none found. Searched the 2021-2024 DA compliance reports (the 2024 report says no market-rate building permits have been submitted), SF YIMBY through Sept 2026, the Chronicle (Jul 29 and Aug 3, 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025) and Potrero View (Oct 2025). SocketSite (Jul 2021) said construction was 'slated to commence in 2023'; SF YIMBY (Mar 2021) said Block 7 construction was expected to start 'by 2023, with completion by 2026'. Neither happened.

Whether the July 2026 Chronicle line 'tallest residential tower would be permitted to reach 248 feet' refers to Block 7A: the D4D allows 240-ft highrise towers on both Block 5 and Block 7, and the amendment package also lets Block 5 flip between residential and commercial. Not confirmed for 7A specifically; the Planning Commission packet for July 30, 2026 was not reviewed.

Unit count drift: 277 (press 2021) -> 325 (approval 2022) -> 319 (compliance reports' LBE appendix); the Planning Commission slides (July 2021) show '315' only on the 'Previous Phase 1' map inside Block 8 and '420' for Block 7 (7A with 7b) on the 'Current Phase 1' slide, so no slide gives a 7A-only count. Which figure a future permit will carry is unknown.

SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says Associate Capital 'will move on to constructing a 300-unit market-rate apartment building' next; the Aug 2026 Chronicle names Block 8 (342 units) as the next building, so 7A does not appear to be next.

Ground-floor childcare (6,000 GSF per DA Phasing Plan) is assigned to Block 7 in the compliance reports; the April 2023 childcare/HPP phasing amendment was not read for this record and may have moved it.
No cost, financing, general contractor or ground-lease information exists for Block 7A in any source found; the land is developer-owned (not Port), so no Port lease applies.

The 'Block 7A' / 'Block 7B' names are the sponsor's; the D4D treats Block 7 as one block with a single 240-ft highrise envelope. This record's map-shape note saying 7A/7B are 'informal press/developer labels' is consistent with the Planning documents, which nonetheless use 7A/7B as case names.

Block 7A rendering (Foster + Partners indicative views from the Design Review Approval packet) removed from the images shown here on 2026-09-29: the plan sheets are marked '(c) Foster + Partners 2020', which is not a licence to host them. records.name: Potrero Power Station Block 9
records.summary: Planned ~240,000-sq-ft, 250-room waterfront hotel site around the Stack and the Unit 3 Power Block (partly demolished in 2023-24; the D4D provides for the hotel with or without Unit 3); the Chronicle reported in May 2025 that the hotel's construction 'could be a decade away' and that the developer proposed an interim park (Prequel Park) on the land instead.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built, and it is not vacant land: it is where the Unit 3 Power Block (partly demolished June 2023 to July 2024 per the 2024 annual compliance report) and the 300-ft Stack stand, and where the interim Prequel Park is planned. No Assessor lot of its own was found: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows its footprint within the much larger active lot 4175028 (1241 Delaware St, about 21,900 sq m, recorded 2022-08-30), which also overlaps the Block 3 and Block 4 footprints. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, positioned by matching several points on it to real streets, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-15m (rebuilt 2026-09-16 with a refined multi-point georeferencing of the site's diagram), and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows this footprint within the much larger active lot 4175028 (1241 Delaware St), not a lot of its own.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) permits Residential, Institutional, Retail (Hotel is permitted, note 10), Non-Retail Sales/Services (office, at the lowest floors only), Entertainment and limited PDR uses on Block 9, and not Laboratory or Life Science. Figure 6.2.3's 'Block 9 Building Configurations' inset shows two alternate massings, by its colour-coded labels: 'with Unit 3' 85 ft, 65 ft and 35 ft plus Unit 3 itself at about 130 ft ('~130''), and 'without Unit 3' 125 ft and 85 ft; the '177'MAX', '110'MAX' and '102'MAX' labels are tick-ended dimension lines, not heights, and Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 9 among the midrise buildings (101-145 ft). This block's real-world area is where Unit 3 and the Stack physically stand (confirmed by the D4D's Standard 6.2.1 and the Chronicle, May 2025; the Stack is mapped separately, as The Stack) and where Prequel Park's approximate interim-park geometry sits (Port Commission memo 10A; also mapped separately, and excluded here via clipping) -- treat this polygon as the block's outer development envelope, not a claim that all of it is buildable independent of those other real features.

The D4D final's Figure 6.2.3 shows a separate 'Block 9 Building Configurations' inset with two alternate massings. By its colour-coded labels, 'with Unit 3' is 85 ft, 65 ft and 35 ft plus Unit 3 itself at about 130 ft ('~130''), and 'without Unit 3' is 125 ft and 85 ft. As described in the 2018 Draft EIR (before Unit 3's abatement and partial demolition, June 2023 to July 2024, per the 2024 annual compliance report): Unit 3 Power Block (128-ft tall steel-frame boiler structure, highest point 143 ft at the elevator shaft, plus a 40-ft tall turbine-generator-condenser structure and a four-story concrete control room building) and the adjacent 300-ft Boiler Stack (mapped separately in this dataset as The Stack)

'Only one rooftop bar shall be permitted on Block 9' under the adopted D4D (Table 3.1.1, note 10); note 7 separately allows rooftop bars on Blocks 2, 3, 11, 12 and 15. The Chronicle (July 29, 2026) describes a rule 'limiting the entire 29-acre development to a single rooftop bar' that the developer asked to eliminate in its 2026 Development Agreement amendment request; the source of that project-wide cap is not identified in the sources found

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is Station A, an existing historic building (the 1901 turbine hall; DBI permit 202406053802 in 2024 describes the unoccupied 'station a building'), so it is not vacant land; the approved vertical addition has not been started. No Assessor lot of its own has been matched to it: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) lists an active, unaddressed lot, 4175026 (recorded 2022-08-30), that overlaps about 85% of this approximate footprint, but that lot has not been confirmed as this block's parcel. The shape was rebuilt on 2026-09-16 with a more careful fit of the diagram to the map, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and corrected again that day after one mis-measured reference point was fixed. notes.regulatory_context: Station A: the site's historic 1901 unreinforced-brick turbine hall (a four-story brick structure per the 2018 Draft EIR), vacant/unoccupied. The design review approves adaptive reuse into approximately 403,750 GSF of office (the Planning Commission granted the office allocation on Oct 22, 2020, Motion 20801) via an eight-story vertical addition above the retained historic shell and a public mid-block passage between Georgia Lane and Power Station Park, designed by Herzog & de Meuron with Adamson Associates; the Planning Director approved the Design Review Application on March 2, 2022. Max height 205 ft total (historic base plus addition), per the Design Review Approval. Construction of the addition had not started per SF YIMBY (Aug 27, 2025) and the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which describes only 2024 brick stabilization work. The 2018 Draft EIR project proposed demolishing Station A (its Alternative D retained it); SF YIMBY (June 2021) says the adaptive reuse was included following community pushback against demolition, and no source found names who advocated for it.

It may be better described as a document than as a single before photo.

The February 17, 2020 photo is shown as a current ('now') view rather than a 'before' view because the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report, submitted March 2025) describes no adaptive-reuse construction on Station A (only 2024 brick stabilization), so the building's exterior likely hasn't changed much since. notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D shows Block 8 with two height limits by its colour-coded labels: 125 ft (along Humboldt and Maryland Streets) and 85 ft (its south-east part); the two '90'MAX' labels are tick-ended dimension lines, not heights (the design-review staff memo describes D4D standard A.8.1 as letting the part of the building above the streetwall extend up to 90 feet in depth from the Humboldt Street and Maryland Street property lines). The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) confirms residential is permitted here (Laboratory and Life Science are not). Foster + Partners is the design architect per the March 2022 design-review approval and the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026). Unit counts differ by source: 249 (SF YIMBY, March 2021), 339 (2022 design-review approval), 342 (Chronicle, Aug 2026). The approved height is about 125 ft to the last occupied floor plus up to 20 ft of screened mechanical (plan set); SF YIMBY reported 140 ft (March 2021) and 156 ft (March 2022). Construction had not started as of the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025); the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) says it is expected to begin in the fall.

records.name: PG&E Southern Switchyard (outside the project boundary; not part of redevelopment)
records.summary: The PG&E Southern Switchyard, one of two PG&E electrical switchyards at the western end of the Potrero Power Station site, shown on the Design for Development's site-boundary figure outside the project site boundary. The other, the roughly 4.8-acre 'PG&E Northern Switchyard' at the corner of 22nd and Illinois Streets, owned and operated by PG&E, is inside the dashed 29-acre planning-area boundary but outside the 21-acre parcel the developer owns and outside the Development Agreement's jurisdiction (this dataset shows that area as Blocks 13 and 14).

notes.accuracy_caveat: LOW CONFIDENCE, DIRECTIONAL ONLY -- this is a materially weaker approximation than this site's numbered blocks. This polygon marks the PG&E Southern Switchyard, which the final D4D (p.12, Figure 1.2.1) places outside the project site boundary, between Humboldt and 23rd Streets west of Block 5. The 4.8-acre PG&E parcel at 22nd and Illinois that public reporting and SF Planning describe is the separate Northern Switchyard, which is inside the project boundary and is not what this polygon shows (this dataset represents that area as Blocks 13 and 14). This polygon's reshaped area is ~4.6 acres, but the D4D gives no area for the Southern Switchyard, so that figure is not a check against anything. The D4D diagram does not further subdivide this area (it is entirely outside the project site boundary, so the D4D had no reason to draw its actual fenceline), so the true switchyard footprint may still differ in detail from this trace. Treat this polygon as marking the correct general block and rough shape (including wrapping around Block 5's south side to 23rd St/Georgia Lane), not the switchyard's real surveyed boundary.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No DataSF Assessor parcel search (by address, by zoning code, or by proximity) turned up a distinctly-shaped, plausibly-switchyard-sized real parcel here -- DataSF's parcel records in this area are either large undifferentiated placeholder shapes (shared across many of this site's D4D blocks, per this dataset's other Potrero entries) or small unrelated lots. Real ownership and the 'not part of the sale' status are well-documented in secondary sources, but a precise Assessor-parcel-level boundary was not found. (This is Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The 2018 draft EIR (Vol. 1, Ch. 2) describes the 4.8-acre PG&E sub-area (the Northern Switchyard) as a portion of Assessor's Block 4175/Lot 018, so an Assessor lot reference exists for that one; none was found for the Southern Switchyard drawn here.
notes.regulatory_context: The PG&E Southern Switchyard: one of two PG&E switchyards at the western end of the Potrero Power Station site (final D4D p.12, Figure 1.2.1), south of the 4.8-acre Northern Switchyard and north of the Transbay Cable site, outside the project site boundary; labelled 'SWITCHYARDS (PG&E)' on Figure 6.2.3, between Illinois Street and Georgia Lane beside Block 5. The 4.8-acre Northern Switchyard at 22nd and Illinois Streets, 'currently owned and operated by PG&E as an electrical switchyard' (SF Planning project page), is a different feature: it is within the 29-acre master plan and the project boundary, and the D4D sets standards for redevelopment of the entire PG&E Sub-area (this dataset represents that area as Blocks 13 and 14). For the Southern Switchyard drawn here, 'outside the project site boundary' is the D4D's statement; the 1990s CPUC divestiture EIR describes a switchyard in the southwest portion of the plant site along the east side of Illinois Street that 'is not part of the sale, and will be retained by PG&E'. Recorded as existing on the strength of the February 2020 D4D showing it; no more recent source was found. 'Commercial' is the nearest category in this map's use list; the feature is an electrical switchyard, a utility use (the D4D's 'Utility and Infrastructure' category), and the map has no utility category.

records.name: The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack)
records.summary: A 300-foot concrete boiler exhaust stack built in 1965 alongside the Unit 3 Power Block; explicitly retained as an existing structure under the Design for Development, and proposed by the developer (May 2025) as a temporary art gallery within the interim Prequel Park.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 marks this with a single point symbol and the label 'STACK / EXISTING STRUCTURE (~300')', not a footprint outline, but this polygon has been rebuilt 2026-09-16 (second revision) to trace the structure's actual visible footprint in satellite imagery (an earlier version read it as a fallen or lowered stack, which no source reports: the D4D, the 2018 Draft EIR and the Chronicle of May 22, 2025 all describe a standing ~300-ft Stack retained by the plan, so the polygon may instead trace the imaged lean of the standing Stack rather than its base; unconfirmed; details are in this shape's mapping log in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record) rather than a diagram-derived placeholder. Treat as accurate to roughly 5-10m -- limited mainly by how precisely the lon/lat grid overlay could be read against the image, not by diagram-transform error.

notes.regulatory_context: The historic ~300 ft tall smokestack from the power station's Unit 3 generating block, called out on the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 as 'EXISTING STRUCTURE (~300')' the plan retains (Standard 6.2.1 sets its height limit at its existing height) -- a literal, physical landmark left standing amid the redevelopment, sitting within Block 9's mapped development envelope (see the Potrero Power Station Block 9 record) at the site's waterfront edge. The Block 9 Building Configurations inset on the same figure shows two alternate massing options labeled 'WITH UNIT 3' and 'WITHOUT UNIT 3' -- meaning the adjacent Unit 3 power block building (distinct from the Stack itself) may or may not be retained; the diagram does not draw Unit 3's own footprint distinctly enough to trace separately, so it is not mapped here as its own feature.

records.summary: Planned ~1.2-acre central park in two blocks either side of Maryland Street: East between Blocks 8 and 12 (multi-purpose lawn and plaza opening to Unit 3 and the Stack) and West between Blocks 7 and 11 (play plaza). Schematic design by Plural Studio was approved by the Planning Director on June 23, 2022 (Case 2017-011878PHA-03). A Phase 1 open space delivered with Blocks 8 (East) and 11 (West); as of the March 2025 annual report neither block nor the park was under construction.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 labels this open space directly but draws it in the final D4D as two plain green rectangles (the one between Blocks 7 and 11 is labelled 'POWER STATION PARK'; an unlabelled one lies between Blocks 8 and 12; Maryland Street runs between them and Block 9 is separate, east of Delaware Street); this is a two-part rectangular approximation (split 2026-09-16 by the real Maryland Street corridor that separates the Block 7/11 side from the Block 8/12 side), a trace of the diagram's rectangles. Each part shares an exact edge with its own two blocks by construction, so accuracy tracks whatever those block shapes carry. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This is Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.)
notes.regulatory_context: The site's central public open space, per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label -- two rectangles, one between Blocks 7 and 11 (labelled 'POWER STATION PARK') and one between Blocks 8 and 12, on either side of Maryland Street; Block 9 lies east of Delaware Street and does not border it. Not yet built: consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) and the SF Chronicle of Aug 3, 2026 (Block 8 construction 'expected to begin in the fall'). Of the blocks around it, Block 7B (the Sophie Maxwell Building) sits 'between Humboldt Street, Maryland Street, Louisiana Paseo and Power Station Park' (2024 annual compliance report) and opened in October 2025 (SF YIMBY, Oct 24, 2025); the others are still planned.

records.summary: Planned shoreline park along the site's Bay frontage: the D4D's ~3.6-acre 'Waterfront Open Spaces' (Waterfront Park with the Blue Greenway, The Point, Stack Plaza, Block 9 plazas and Humboldt Street Plaza), which SF Planning summarizes as a ~3-acre waterfront park opening over 1,000 linear feet of shoreline. About 2 acres of the project's open space is on Port-owned shoreline property leased under L-16662 (66 years, $1/year), with BCDC permit 2019.006 issued July 2021. Delivery is phased (Waterfront Park South before the certificate of occupancy for 3 million sq ft; The Point before 500,000 sq ft; North/West with Block 4); The Point's design review has been pending since Dec 2021, and the interim Prequel Park precedes the permanent park.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 labels this as a long, curving shoreline strip running the full length of the site's bay frontage (continuing north and south beyond this figure's own page crop in the source PDF). This polygon traces only the portion visible on Figure 6.2.3 itself as a simplified strip (not the full shoreline extent, and not precisely following the actual curving shore/site-boundary line, which was simplified to a handful of vertices). Treat as directionally correct but incomplete and shape-approximate. Same 15-25m positional tolerance as this site's other entries. Position corrected 2026-09-15 (12m uniform shift onto the real shoreline, see the mapping log in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record)) -- the strip's own curve/shape still was not independently re-verified vertex-by-vertex against the coastline, only its overall position. Second position correction 2026-09-15: re-traced directly from satellite imagery color (water vs. land pixel classification), not the diagram transform -- now an 8m-wide ribbon on the real shoreline, including the southern point/breakwater curve. Still simplified (does not capture the D4D-labeled strips full north-south extent beyond what is visible here) and the exact width (8m) is an assumption, not measured from any park-design source. NOTE 2026-09-16: this feature's own outer-shoreline trace turned out to substantially overlap the newly-added 'Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)' -- evidence (a Spring 2026 construction-pipeline listing describing the same corridor as a '2-acre Waterfront Park', which could not be located or checked) suggests both features describe the same physical shoreline strip: this one as the D4D's own long-term planning label, Prequel Park as the interim park (still planned: the Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 says the developer hoped to start construction in the third quarter of 2026, and no source confirms a start). The overlap is expected, not a tracing error -- see Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)'s own mapping log. Not merged into one feature since the two have different sourcing/status and either could be independently corrected later.

records.name: Humboldt Street Plaza
records.summary: Planned small, mostly paved flexible-use plaza between Blocks 4 and 9 at the foot of Humboldt Street, giving a car-free connection from Delaware Street to the Blue Greenway and a waterside Bay overlook terrace (D4D 4.24, 4.19.2). A Phase 2 open space due before the first certificate of occupancy for the building representing 3 million sq ft of development; no design review or construction has been reported.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 labels this open space directly, shown as a small plaza area between Block 4 (north) and Block 9 (south). This polygon is a simplified rectangular approximation of that labeled area, built directly from the mapped corners of Block 4 and Block 9 (see the mapping log) so it shares an exact edge with both -- its accuracy is that of those two blocks' shapes. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This reflects Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.)
notes.regulatory_context: A small public plaza per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label, between Block 4 and Block 9 near the site's waterfront edge.

facts.value: California Barrel Company LLC (project sponsor); now Fifth Space (formerly Associate Capital)

'open and flexible space, primarily paved', for open-air markets, performances, public art and interpretive exhibits; required amenities: seating, lighting, open flexible-use plaza space, planted areas, bicycle parking, waste receptacles, power for temporary markets and performances; 26-foot emergency vehicle access between Blocks 4 and 9 from Delaware Street
Block 4 (north) and Block 9 (south); waterside Bay Overlook Terrace at Humboldt Street Plaza continues the plaza paving across the Blue Greenway (D4D 4.19.2)
Phase 2 (DA originally Phase 1); delivered before the first certificate of occupancy for the building representing 3 million sq ft of total development

IMP: 26-foot fire access for 150 feet from Delaware Street and 20-foot emergency access to the waterfront; sits over a public utility easement; conceptual stormwater outfall at Humboldt Street Plaza (IMP Figure 15.4); overland release option where streets meet the plaza
Owned and maintained by the Project Master Association (IMP 9.2)

The interim Prequel Park (mapped by Pier & Point as a Power Station sub-area) shares edges with this plaza; whether the interim park occupies the plaza's footprint is not shown in any scaled drawing reviewed.
BOS File 260724 (Amended and Restated DA, 2026) amends the Phasing Plan; possible changes to this plaza's phase were not checked (draft DA not read).

No designer of Humboldt Street Plaza is named in any source found: in the final D4D, CMG Landscape Architecture appears only as a photo credit on precedent images (Figure 4.24.4 and elsewhere), not as the plaza's designer, and no design review application exists for the plaza.

The Chronicle reported that no plans for a data center appeared to have been filed with the city as of that report.

The background layer has not yet been extended. That this is a real Assessor parcel rests on DataSF Parcels (acdm-wktn), which lists blklot 4241004 as an active parcel addressed 1215 MICHIGAN; the Chronicle article names the address but does not discuss the parcel.

records.name: Mission Creek Park
records.summary: A waterfront park along Mission Creek in Mission Bay (SF Rec & Park lists it as Mission Creek Park (North and South), bordered by Berry Street to the north and west and Channel Street to the south, ending at 3rd Street), labeled P2 and P3 -- and, for its amphitheater feature, P1 -- on OCII's current Mission Bay South open-space page; its P1 segment was among the first Mission Bay parks to open (2002, per SF Rec & Park's Workshop 3 timeline). The San Francisco Recreation and Park Department assumed management and maintenance of the park on July 1, 2023. No source checked gives the surrounding park landscaping's own original construction or opening date, as distinct from the separately dated Mission Creek Park Pavilion within it (see that record).

notes.accuracy_caveat: HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon (matches SF Rec & Park's own facility listing). Other OSM ways (579664205 further east, and 27369705) may cover parts of this same park; they are not cited and had not been checked as of September 2026; this feature uses the single most detailed, currently-tagged way covering the park's main extent along Mission Creek's south bank. A later revision could merge the full multi-segment shoreline extent. Updated 2026-09-20: now a MultiPolygon that also includes P1, P2 and P8's geometry (P1 a separate segment further along the same north/west bank; P2/P8 real scraps of land on the creek's opposite/south-east bank, not contiguous with this record's original OSM shape). Each sub-piece keeps its own sourcing/confidence as documented in its own original record (P1, P2, P8) -- this union does not upgrade their confidence to this record's own 'HIGH CONFIDENCE, real OSM' rating.

open_questions: The 2019-09 and 2022-10 milestones are both for the P3 extension specifically (a 1.2-1.65-acre addition extending the park toward China Basin Park; Potrero View puts the existing Mission Creek Park west of Fourth Street and does not say the extension is), not the original park. The Potrero View source's fall-2021 target (after a COVID-19 pause) did not hold -- the Landscape Performance Series case study gives an actual completion date of October 2022, about a year later.

No source checked gives Mission Creek Park's own original construction/opening date; the Mission Creek Park Pavilion within it has a separately sourced 2003 completion (see the Mission Creek Park Pavilion record), but that doesn't establish when the surrounding park landscaping itself opened -- background reading (a Southeast Waterfront community history page, and a landscape-architecture magazine mention of a 2004-dated EDAW site-plan rendering seen only in a search-result summary, not confirmed against the actual article text) suggested an early-2000s completion but nothing specific enough to cite as a fact.

OCII's September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists plan parcels P1, P3, P5, P6, P10, P11/11A, P16, P17 and P26 as already RPD-managed by that date, but lists 'P2/P8' among parcels RPD 'will manage ... when built' (i.e., not yet complete as of Sept 2023) -- this record's own mapping log separately documents a 2026-09-20 union with P2 and P8 as 'barely touch[ing] this record's original shape,' consistent with those specific pieces being a later, smaller addition rather than part of the original park; not used to date the union since the two documents describe different things (a funding/management list vs. a geometry merge).

OCII's plan-label usage for this park is inconsistent across documents over time: the Nov 2024 CAC deck labels the whole feature 'P3'; the current sfocii.org open-space page splits it into P1 (amphitheater), P2 and P3; and a 2015 Successor Agency LRPMP (cited on Pier & Point's neighboring P7/P8/P9 records) uses P2, P7, P8 and P9 for nearby, separately tracked open-space parcels along the same creek. Not reconciled here.

The groundbreaking article (SF YIMBY, Aug 10, 2022) says the ceremony was 'held last week,' so early August 2022 is used rather than a specific day; the article's own stated completion target (fall 2023) was superseded by the actual October 2024 opening, which is not itself explained in any source checked.

The notes on this record's map shape say the park occupies the Mission Bay South Design Controls Plan's former P21/P22 open-space parcels; OCII's own September 2023 open-space transition presentation (sfocii.org, Item 2) lists P21 as already Port-managed by that date but P22 as still 'when built' -- consistent with part of the site predating this park's 2024 completion, but not independently broken out here.

An earlier version of this record named '16th Street Plaza' as the venue for the October 22, 2024 celebration; that was removed because the SF.gov release names no plaza as the venue, saying only that the park has multiple plazas.

Precise month of this block's actual completion/first occupancy is not sourced beyond the bare Assessor year.
Developer of record beyond BRE Properties/Essex Property Trust, and any subsequent sale history: not yet researched.

The Registry's own article (already cited above) reports BRE Properties 'expected a total development cost of $227 million, or $630,000 a unit' -- but that figure covers the whole 360-unit, two-block MB360 development (this record's 701 China Basin St block plus the separate 1200 4th St block) as one project, not this 188-unit block alone. No block-specific figure was found, so no record-scope figure is added here.

The Apartments.com listing could not be checked on 2026-09-29; an archived copy exists at web.archive.org/web/20211031174227/https://www.apartments.com/mb360-san-francisco-ca/bzdysc8/ (not checked). The 701 China Basin St address is confirmed by the Assessor and OSM.

records.name: J. David Gladstone Institutes
records.summary: The J. David Gladstone Institutes' Mission Bay headquarters at 1650 Owens Street: a six-story, roughly 200,000-sq-ft biomedical research building for this independent nonprofit research organization (in academic partnership with UCSF), dedicated in December 2004. The expansion of the six-story building from 200,000 to 275,000 sq ft (about 75,000 sq ft added, around $160 million) was announced in February 2023, with construction then expected to start in late 2024 and finish by 2026; whether it was built is not confirmed. In March 2026 Gladstone announced more than 105,000 sq ft of future lab space in a new building at 1450 Owens Street, opening in early 2027.

records.summary: Three buildings tracked as one combined record (the two mapped footprints share DataSF Building Footprints id SF3940003, whose parcels are addressed 409 and 499 Illinois St; which footprint is 490 Illinois St is unresolved): UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision, a 347,500-sq-ft, 12-story eye-care tower at 490 Illinois Street that SF YIMBY reported open on November 27, 2020, at a reported cost of about $237 million (SmithGroup architect); 499 Illinois Street, a 6-story biotechnology building (its structural engineer describes a 500,000 sq ft center in two buildings) completed 2008 and owned by Alexandria Real Estate Equities until UCSF bought it; and 409 Illinois Street, which Alexandria also owned and which UCSF bought together with 499 Illinois St for $767,000,000 in December 2025 and is renovating into its new School of Dentistry and an Interprofessional Education Center, targeted to open in late 2029.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed DataSF Building Footprints outline (mblr SF3940003), names/addresses from OpenStreetMap; not a hand trace or plan estimate. UCSF's own occupancy at 499 Illinois St (leased space and 90% of the building, then bought it with 409 Illinois St from Alexandria in Dec 2025, per SF Standard 2025-12-17) versus outright ownership at 490 Illinois St is not distinguished in this single combined record -- each wing's own mapping history is logged in this shape's data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). As of 2026-09-29, which OSM way and footprint is 490 versus 499 Illinois St is unresolved.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF3940003); names/addresses from OpenStreetMap ways 84821715 (490 Illinois St) and 84821722 (499 Illinois St).

facts.value: 490 Illinois St (Valley Center for Vision): SmithGroup. 409 Illinois St renovation (School of Dentistry / Interprofessional Education Center): CO Architects, with Suffolk as design-build contractor.

490 Illinois St: 347,500 across three separate buildings (12-story tower, 5-story south wing, 3-story north wing) plus ~75,000 sq ft of parking for 200+ vehicles. 499 Illinois St: six stories per its 2006 DBI permit (its structural engineer, SGH, describes two five-story buildings over two levels of parking); size reported variously -- SGH: a 500,000 sq ft center in two buildings; SF Standard (2025): 409 and 499 together add up to 470,000 sq ft. 409 and 499 Illinois St combined (per UC's own Dec 2025 acquisition filing): ~525,421 rentable sq ft on 3.6 acres with a 587-space shared garage. 409 Illinois St's renovation into the School of Dentistry / Interprofessional Education Center is 261,117 gross sq ft.

490 Illinois St: opened for the University of California, San Francisco (SF YIMBY); fundraising led by the nonprofit That Man May See. 499 Illinois St: owned by Alexandria Real Estate Equities (its 2013 release calls it 'Alexandria's 499 Illinois Street'; sold to UC in Dec 2025 per SF Standard); no source read states who developed it.

409 Illinois St: 3940003. 499 Illinois St: 3940005 per DataSF's current Assessor parcel data (queried 2026-09-28) -- differs from the block/lot 001 the 2006 building permit used and the lot 004 an earlier source in this record cites; the Assessor's own lot numbering for this address has clearly changed more than once and is not fully reconciled here (see the open questions). 490 Illinois St's own blklot was not re-confirmed.

open_questions: MERGED 2026-09-22: this record combines the former separate 490 Illinois St and 499 Illinois St records, matching the 2026-09-22 merge of their map shapes -- both buildings share one DataSF Building Footprints mblr (SF3940003) and are described together as a connected 490-499 Illinois campus in commercial listings. UCSF's own occupancy at 499 Illinois St (leased, then purchased) versus outright ownership at 490 Illinois St is not distinguished by a source found as of 2026-09-29.

Exact opening day within November 2020 (490 Illinois) is not given by the source found; only the month is confirmed. Exact month/day of the 2008 completion (499 Illinois) is likewise not sourced, only the year.

The 2006 construction permit's own block/lot for 499 Illinois St (block 3940, lot 001) differs from the lot the Assessor now uses for this address (lot 004); the address, biotechnical/medical-research-facility description, 6 stories, and $90M cost all line up with this parcel, so this is treated as a lot renumbering, not a different building. The permit's own completion sign-off (2009-04-06) also runs slightly later than the Assessor's 2008 year, which may reflect a lag between substantial completion and permit closeout.

Found on 2026-09-21: the January 26, 2017 Regents budget/design approval item for 490 Illinois St (UCSF calls it 'Block 33' in its own campus numbering -- assumed at the time to be a coincidental name collision with this project's unrelated OCII-plan block 33). The ucsf.edu article itself could not be read directly; its content (matching $237,000,000 cost and 12-story/5-story/3-story massing figures already in this record) was confirmed via a search-engine summary rather than a direct read. A primary Regents PDF for the January 26, 2017 item itself was not located.

2026-09-22: the 'coincidental name collision' assumption above was reopened -- Pier & Point identified OCII plan block 33 (the UCSF Valley Center for Vision west building record, west of Illinois St, about 60-100m from this record's 490 Illinois St tower) as ALSO being Valley Center for Vision, not unrelated. Whether that west building is a second wing of this same facility, a distinct building sharing the name, or a misidentification, is unresolved -- see that record's own open questions; not re-investigated here.
No opening date found for Caffe Central (490 Illinois St): checked its own site for a firm date; retail_confirmed.csv's own opened field is also blank, and the building itself only opened Nov 2020.

2026-09-28: exact month/day for 409 Illinois St's 2026 renovation start, and the exact date within 'late 2029' targeted for completion, are not given by any source found. Whether the Construction Dive-reported $278,000,000 figure is Suffolk's construction contract value alone or the total project cost (design, FF&E, etc.) is also not stated by that source. No SF Planning case number exists for this renovation because UC, as a state entity, is exempt from local planning review -- all environmental review runs through UC itself as CEQA lead agency; treat the absence of a Planning case number as confirmed, not unresearched. The Assessor's blklot for 499 Illinois St has been given as 3940001 (2006 permit), 3940004 (an earlier source in this record) and now 3940005 (a live 2026-09-28 query) -- not reconciled here; possibly repeated lot-line adjustments on a shared master parcel with 409 Illinois St, whose current blklot (3940003) is comparatively well-confirmed.

As of 2026-09-29: (a) OpenStreetMap tags way 84821715 as 499 Illinois St and way 84821722 as 490 Illinois St (both 6 levels, 28 m, source Yahoo), the opposite of the labels used for this record's map shape; DataSF Parcels (acdm-wktn) list lots 3940003 (409 Illinois), 3940004 (499) and 3940005 (409-499) under mapblklot 3940003 and none addressed 490, so the shared mblr SF3940003 is a 409/499 pairing. Which mapped footprint is the 490 Illinois St Vision Center is unresolved and still to be settled against satellite imagery. (b) The UCSF news page for the January 2017 Regents approval could not be read and the Regents date is unconfirmed. (c) SF YIMBY (2020-11-27) shows the Vision Center open by that date but gives no opening date. (d) No source read says who developed 499 Illinois St, or that UCSF leased 'for over a decade'; SF Standard (2025-12-17) says UCSF leased space and occupied 90% of the building before buying it.

records.name: P2

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE, AND KNOWINGLY DISPLACED -- one of the two pieces making up this shape (the paved path further southeast) really lies about 17-22 m south of where it is drawn here; Pier & Point shifted it on purpose to close a real gap (a planting/tree strip between two paved features) with a single deliberate move rather than tracing that gap's own edges. The other piece (the strip along the creek's near bank) is a computed shape bounded by streets, the creek and neighbouring mapped shapes, not hand-traced. Overlaps the existing 'Mission Creek Park' shape (which Pier & Point intends to merge with this record and P8, on the view that Mission Creek Park will grow to cover P1+P2+P8) and may overlap the Mission Creek Park -- east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge) record (P1) at its northeast end, near the edge of the area searched for open ground -- not reconciled with either. Deliberately not trimmed back from the street lines: this record includes area covering today's paved road across the corridor (a park-corridor concept, not today's satellite extent) -- the same kind of exception as Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza. This is not a mispositioned trace; it is an intentional choice to keep the corridor continuous rather than split by a road the park is meant to cross at grade.
notes.digitized_from: Traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street centerlines and all neighbouring mapped shapes along the creek corridor between Mission Creek and Channel St, which left a set of separate scraps of unclaimed land. records.notes: OCII plan parcel P2. Runs along the near (south/west) bank of Mission Creek between the creek and Channel St, from about where P8 hands off near the Mission Bay Circle roundabout, northeast toward the creek bend. open_questions: No independently published source dates when this specific stretch was built; it was hand-traced from satellite imagery because it was visibly already landscaped, not because any source dated its construction.

This record's own mapping log says OCII's plan labels P1 and P3 both fall somewhere in this general stretch, based on its reading of the Nov 2024 CAC 'Remaining Mission Bay Open Space Parcels Update' -- but that deck's own extractable text only labels the whole wider park 'Mission Creek Park (P3)' and does not break out a separate P1 sub-area within this specific reach; which label (if either) applies to this exact segment, versus to the separately tracked Mission Creek Park record's own P1 (an amphitheater, per OCII's current open-space page), is not resolved.
Name/operator: presumed to be part of the same SF Recreation and Park Department-managed Mission Creek Park system as its neighbors, but not independently confirmed for this specific segment.

As of 2026-09-22, flagged rather than resolved: this record is currently classified 'Mission Bay South' and its own sourcing leans on Mission Bay South's P1/P3 plan labels (see above). But this record's own coordinates sit at the same latitude as other already-tracked Mission Bay North records (The Beacon, Rich Sorro Commons), north of the core of the separately tracked, South-side Mission Creek Park record. A landscape architecture firm's own project page (Munden Fry Landscape Associates, mflastudio.com/mission-creek-park-north) independently describes real, differently-numbered 'NP1 Mission Creek Park Promenade' and 'NP2 Mission Creek Park' parcels for Catellus, built 1999-2011, on Mission Creek's north bank -- a description (residential to the north, the creek and a houseboat community to the south) that matches this record's own traced bank. Whether this segment is actually part of Mission Bay North's NP1/NP2 system rather than South's P1/P3 is an open identity question bigger than a date, not resolved here -- flagged for a closer look, possibly including whether this record's site classification itself should change.

Corrected 2026-09-29: the summary previously said this stretch is on Mission Creek's north/west bank; the traced polygon sits on the Channel St side (south/east bank), as does the Pavilion, and OCII's Nov 2024 map shows the P1 label on the south-bank strip. Berry St, the north bank, is about 200 m away.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- satellite trace by Pier & Point, idealized to a fitted semicircle rather than left as a raw hand-traced outline. open_questions: Pier & Point first identified the building here as UCSF Neurosurgery at Mission Bay from its own knowledge (correcting an earlier mis-resolution to Genentech Hall), and at first that identification was not independently corroborated by a primary source. Later research found strong, independent corroboration: a contractor project page names this same OCII Block 23A as the site of the Joan and Sanford I. Weill Neurosciences Building, and UCSF Health's own clinic-location page places its 'Neurosurgery Mission Bay - Fourth St.' service at 1651 4th Street, the Weill building's address, directly adjacent to Third Street Garage as this record's geometry describes. Not treated as fully closed: no single source explicitly ties the parcel-level footprint to the 1651 4th Street address by lot number.

Exact opening day is not confirmed: this record uses October 2021 (from UCSF's own news article, dated by its URL and by architecture-press coverage of the same announcement); one secondary aggregation suggested October 28, 2021 specifically, but that day was not independently verified against a primary page.

Construction cost is reported elsewhere (via a $185 million naming gift from the Weill Family Foundation, and a total project value cited by some outlets around $535 million) but was not independently verified against a primary UCSF or Regents document, so left out of costs.

The March 2016 Regents preliminary-plans item (270,000 gsf, six stories) predates the Weill naming gift and 'Weill Neurosciences Building' name; identification with this record rests on the Block 23A site match (confirmed elsewhere in this record's own sources), not a name match in the 2016 item itself.

The opening month shown is July 2021, as UCSF Health's own Weill page says ('It opened its doors in July 2021'); the UCSF news release dated 2021-10 (which could not be checked) was earlier cited for October 2021 and is likely an announcement date. The March 2016 Regents item planned full budget approval for March 2017 while the UCSF news release cited for the $357.6 million budget (which also could not be checked) is dated May 2017, so that schedule slipped; the primary Regents item for the budget was not found (the Regents' March and May 2017 meeting materials were looked for without success). The March 2016 item is an agenda item requesting approval; the minutes recording the vote were not read.

Boundary is the edge of the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes (following the estimated curb radius), with one corner redrawn to the real street angle (see the mapping log), not a hand-traced or surveyed building footprint. OPEN QUESTION, not resolved: this project also tracks a separate, already-committed record named 'Valley Center for Vision' at 490 Illinois St, about 60-100m east of this polygon, across Illinois St. UCSF's own map names block 33 (this building, between 3rd St and Illinois St) as the Valley Center for Vision, so it is the 490 Illinois St record whose label may be wrong; the two records have not yet been reconciled -- flagged here rather than silently merged or changed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).

open_questions: This project already tracks a separate, independently sourced record also named Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois St (the 490/499 Illinois Street record), about 60-100m east of this building, across Illinois St. That record's own 2017 UC Regents source describes a single 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing and a 3-story north wing at 490 Illinois St -- it does not mention a separate west-of-Illinois-St building. Whether this west building is a second wing/annex of the same named facility built later, a distinct building that happens to share the name, or a misidentification of one of the two records, has not been resolved against any primary source -- flagged here rather than silently merged with, or silently treated as unrelated to, the 490 Illinois St record.

2026-09-22, new data point (not a resolution): matching DataSF's business-registration records to this building's shape by location, after the shape was added to the map, shows several registrations -- Buenafe #2, All May See, All May See Foundation, Simon Fung -- whose registered point-location falls inside THIS west building's polygon, but whose own listed street address is '490 Illinois St' (the other, east-of-Illinois-St tower's address), not a west-of-Illinois-St address. This could mean the two buildings genuinely share one administrative/mailing address, or it could simply be a DataSF geocoding artifact (a coarse or shared geocode for a multi-building campus) -- the match is by location only and is never treated as confirmed on its own, so this is logged as a data point for later review, not treated as confirming the relationship either way. Notably, the same matching for the neighboring UCSF Bayfront Medical Building and UCSF Illinois Street Garage records do show addresses consistent with their own already-sourced identities (520 Illinois St and 590 Illinois St respectively), which is corroborating, not contradictory, evidence for those two.

No address, opening date, architect, cost or square footage for this specific west building was found as of 2026-09-22; every fact this project has for 'Valley Center for Vision' construction, cost and massing lives in the 490 Illinois St record instead, and may or may not apply here.

Geometry: this building's east edge (its own real, digitized boundary) sits close to, but not necessarily exactly on, Illinois St's west curb line -- not independently verified against DataSF Building Footprints or an Assessor parcel; see the shape's accuracy caveat.

Added 2026-09-29: UCSF's June 12, 2025 CAC presentation (p.3 map, updated December 2024) labels block 33, between Third St and Illinois St, 'VALLEY CENTER FOR VISION (33)', which supports this record's identification. That reverses the open question above: the separate 490/499 Illinois St record, whose polygon is east of the Illinois St centerline, may be the one that is mislabelled as Valley Center for Vision. The two records have not yet been reconciled; nothing was changed here.

records.summary: A 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and maintenance facility at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square, including the existing 4th & King Street Station itself. Owned by Prologis, with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP); Prologis has floated a development concept of up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total (about half commercial), anchored by a tower as tall as 850 feet (SF Standard, March 2026); a Development Agreement is the expected approval path, the same one used for Pier 70, Mission Rock and Potrero Power Station.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- not a surveyed parcel or a GIS file from Caltrain/Prologis/SF Planning. Correction (2026-09-29): this polygon is not free of Assessor parcels. DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset (as of 2026-05-31) carries three active secured-roll parcels lying wholly inside it (8701004, 700 4th St; 8701003, 311 Townsend St; 8700001, 797 7th St; together about 82% of its area), so the earlier statement that the rail right-of-way carries no block/lot was wrong. It stays an approximate feature here; whether it should instead be mapped as real parcels has not yet been decided. Three of the four sides (Townsend, 4th, 7th) are real, continuous DataSF street centerlines; the fourth (King St plus a straight closing line at the I-280 interchange, drawn on the earlier belief that King's DataSF centerline ended short of 7th; see the correction to how this shape was traced) is the weakest edge and the one most likely to need revision if a real project boundary or EIR figure becomes available. Includes the existing Caltrain 4th & King Street Station itself, which the project's own description treats as part of the site being redeveloped, not something outside it.
notes.digitized_from: Bounded by DataSF's official street centerlines: Townsend St (4th-7th) on the north, 4th St (Townsend-King) on the east, 7th St (Townsend-King) on the west, and King St (4th-~6th) on the south, each widened by the standard measured half-width used across this map (6.8m) and inset from the outer street-to-street ring by that same half-width to approximate the curb/yard edge rather than the street centerline itself -- the same method as P9. Correction (2026-09-29): the earlier text here said King St's DataSF centerline stops short of 7th St. It does not: the dataset has King St segments from 6th to 7th St (06TH ST -> 07TH ST, (-122.398585, 37.77289) to (-122.400804, 37.771138), plus '06TH ST - END: WEST' and 'END: EAST - 07TH ST' pieces); only the 5th-6th St segment ends at (-122.397986, 37.773324), and the next segment begins about 70 m further on. I-280 ramp segments are in the dataset too. The southern closing edge was drawn as a straight line from that 5th-6th point to 7th St's King-St corner and has not been re-checked against the 6th-7th St King segments (the geometry is unchanged). The resulting inset polygon is 20.08 acres, matching the SF Planning/Caltrain FAQ's own '20-acre site' description almost exactly, and its outline was checked directly against an overlay on Esri World Imagery -- it tracks the real fan of tracks and the 4th & King station platform canopy tightly, confirmed by Pier & Point on 2026-09-21 after a side-by-side review of the overlay.

records.summary: An 18,064-to-19,500-seat arena for the Golden State Warriors (NBA) and Golden State Valkyries (WNBA, since 2025), anchoring an 11-acre, privately financed mixed-use development in Mission Bay with 580,000 sq ft of office/lab space (Uber and the Warriors each lease office space in the adjacent towers for their headquarters, per The Real Deal, 2025), 100,000 sq ft of retail (branded "Thrive City" on Chase Center's own site) and a 35,000 sq ft public plaza; designed by MANICA Architecture with Gensler (interiors), built by a Mortenson/Clark Construction joint venture, and opened September 6, 2019.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, DERIVED BOUNDARY -- the outer edge is a real DataSF Assessor Parcel boundary (blklot 8722025); the two notches cut into its NW and SW corners are real OpenStreetMap building traces (the Uber towers), not estimates. The resulting shape has not been independently verified against a surveyed Chase Center site plan -- it is real-minus-real, not a single authoritative source. Two small structures inside this polygon (an oval building in the west plaza, and possibly others) remain unidentified. The shape is deliberately not trimmed to DataSF's official street centerlines: that layer shows several stale/closed street segments cutting straight through the arena bowl itself (visible as a literal cross running under the roof when the shape is drawn against the street lines) -- leftover records from the four separate plan blocks (29/30/31/32) that were consolidated into one superblock when Chase Center was built, not real current streets. Trimming against them would remove 16% of this polygon's real area, so it is left untrimmed for this stated reason, as is Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza.

open_questions: 2026-09-23: this record's map shape was moved off its Assessor parcel record (the record was previously keyed to block/lot 8722025) because DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives this parcel and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 towers byte-identical geometry (one shared master-condo superblock parcel). The new geometry is the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' own real OSM building footprints subtracted out; how it was built is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). Two small structures inside the resulting polygon are not yet identified: an oval building in the west plaza, and possibly others not yet checked against satellite imagery.

Chase Center's cost: $1.4B is the most-repeated figure (Construction Dive's headline and Wikipedia's infobox). A $1.3B alternate figure attributed to a Warriors executive had no support in its cited source and was removed on 2026-09-29. A separate 2019 Construction Dive piece on the (distinct, unbuilt) hotel/condo proposal used '$1.5B Chase Center' in its own headline, which appears to conflate the arena with that proposal; that figure is not used here.

Uber's and the Warriors' current lease status was not independently verified beyond The Real Deal's February 2025 report; an earlier '20-year lease', '~4,000 employees' and '145 parking spaces' claim was removed on 2026-09-29 because no readable source states it.

The Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex on adjacent Blocks 29-30 is financially and physically tied to Chase Center but may sit on a separate parcel; whether it falls within blklot 8722025 or is a distinct, not-yet-built record is not confirmed. Current 2026 construction status is also unconfirmed.

No primary Port of San Francisco or OCII page dedicated specifically to Chase Center was found (as a privately financed project, it may not have one); the only agency-level source found was SFPUC/CleanPowerSF's sustainability write-up.
No openly licensed image was found; recommend linking rather than hosting until one is confirmed.
No opening date found for The Sarap Shop (1 Warriors Way): checked its own Thrive City vendor page for a firm date; retail_confirmed.csv's own opened field is also blank.

As of 2026-09-29: the first photo (exterior, taken 2019-07-27) shows the arena under construction, before the 2019-09-06 opening milestone, so it fits none of the image categories used here; it keeps the 'now' category pending a decision. The interior photo (2019-12-27) was re-tagged 'completed' (within a year after opening). Chase Center's Thrive City tenant list was read on its live page on 2026-09-29 ('Open Now'); tenants not on it (Siren, b8ta, Mission Bay Wine Bar) have not been re-confirmed open.

open_questions: On 2026-09-23 this record's map shape was moved off the Assessor parcel (block/lot 8722063; the record was renamed accordingly) because DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives this parcel and the neighboring Chase Center arena identical geometry (one shared master-condo superblock parcel). The shape is now the union of both towers' own real OpenStreetMap building footprints (OSM ways 1410182008 and 1410183655). How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).

Uber's SEC EDGAR company record lists 1725 3rd Street as its business address (read 2026-09-29), though a May 2023 SF Standard report said that specific building had never been occupied by Uber and was being marketed for sublease -- current occupancy is genuinely unclear and not resolved here.

DataSF business-registration data shows several Uber-internal registrations here (Bon Appetit @ Uber cafeteria service across multiple floors, Uber Freight Holding Corporation, a Mercedes-Benz-branded garage/showroom) not yet researched or added as facts.
No dedicated primary source (an Alexandria or Uber press release specifically) was found for the exact completion date of each tower individually; 2021 is used as a combined year.

No total development or construction cost for the two towers was found as of 2026-09-23. records.summary: Two Port-owned floating dry docks at Piers 68 & 70 -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- that the Port Commission declared an emergency over on 2025-12-08 after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding caused Dry Dock No. 2 to list. notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a coarse placeholder box, not a traced footprint. This is a Port tideland facility with no Assessor parcel and no source site plan or GIS shapefile was found to digitize the actual dry-dock basins, cranes and sheds from. The box is anchored to two real points (the 20th/Illinois St intersection, and the narrow real gap between Pier 70's and Mission Bay South's own tracked geometry) but does not represent the true shape or full extent of the 13-acre shipyard, which projects east into the Bay beyond what a land-based box can show. Needs replacement with a real digitized footprint if a Port GIS layer or the Dry Dock Memorandum's own site figure becomes available.
notes.digitized_from: No Assessor block/lot exists for this Port tideland/water-lot facility (confirmed: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' Socrata dataset, acdm-wktn, has no PIER-numbered street_name entries at all near this site, consistent with pier and dry-dock structures sitting outside the Assessor's secured roll). No Port GIS shapefile or site-plan figure for the Piers 68/70 shipyard footprint was available to digitize from directly, so this is a coarse locational box only, centered near the shipyard's known entrance at 20th and Illinois St (a real intersection in DataSF's official street centerlines) and sized to sit between the tracked Pier 70 parcel's own northern edge (Crane Cove Park, max latitude 37.76406) and Mission Bay South's nearest tracked features (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage and the P24 waterfront lawn, both of which reach south to roughly latitude 37.7644-37.7648) -- the real Piers 68/70 shipyard, described in Port materials as a 13-acre facility at the 'northeast corner' of the complex including Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock, occupies this narrow shoreline gap and extends east into the Bay itself, which this box does not attempt to trace.

records.distance_note: Piers 38 and 40, at the foot of King St/Townsend St (89 King St), sit about 420-460m north of Mission Rock's own tracked boundary (Pier 48/50), just north of and adjacent to South Beach Harbor.

how_to_comment.channel: Port of San Francisco project page

records.summary: A long-stalled Port of San Francisco redevelopment of Piers 38 and 40, led by San Francisco Waterfront Partners (an affiliate of Pacific Waterfront Partners). The original 2021 Exclusive Negotiating Agreement expired in 2023 after missed performance dates; in April 2026 the Port Commission settled a related back-rent dispute and adopted an Amended and Restated ENA giving the developer a 12-month "Evaluation Period" to rework the project's scope and financing. No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's last_verified date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a coarse placeholder box (the union of the two piers' real OpenStreetMap-sourced bounding boxes), not a traced footprint of the pier structures themselves, since no parcel or source figure exists for this Port facility -- see digitized_from. It does not represent the true shape or extent of either pier, only their combined location. Needs replacement with a real digitized footprint if a Port GIS layer or site-plan figure becomes available.
notes.digitized_from: No Assessor block/lot exists for this Port pier facility (confirmed: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' Socrata dataset, acdm-wktn, has no PIER-numbered street_name entries). No Port GIS shapefile or site-plan figure was available. CORRECTED 2026-09-30: the box's location is now the union of OpenStreetMap's own two named building entries for the piers -- 'Pier 40' (way 104599990, bounding box lat 37.7815294-37.7819100, lon -122.3870563--122.3855684) and 'Pier 38' (way 104599982, bounding box lat 37.7818929-37.7829023, lon -122.3879887--122.3847049), both confirmed via OpenStreetMap Nominatim on 2026-09-30 -- not a traced footprint of either building, just their combined location, since no Port GIS figure or site plan exists to trace from.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Port pier facility; not on the Assessor's secured roll (data.sf.gov acdm-wktn has no PIER-numbered parcels near this site).
notes.regulatory_context: Developer: San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP), an affiliate of Pacific Waterfront Partners (PWP). Original Exclusive Negotiating Agreement: Port Commission Resolution 21-10 (2021-02-23), expired 2023-03-15 for missed performance dates. PWP separately owed the Port over $980,000 in back rent on three unrelated leases (Pier 28, two Agriculture Building suites), unpaid since it vacated them 2024-01-31. On 2026-04-28 the Port Commission adopted a Settlement Agreement (Resolution 26-21: PWP to pay $720,000 over 3 years, with the remainder of the debt forgiven on compliance) and an Amended and Restated ENA (Resolution 26-22: a 12-month 'Evaluation Period' to explore value engineering, project phasing and a new financial partner, with a new Schedule of Performance due before the period ends around April 2027). No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's own last_verified date.

open_questions: No Port Commission agenda item after 2026-04-28 was found; the 12-month Evaluation Period runs to approximately April 2027 with an interim Schedule of Performance due before then -- worth a periodic re-check rather than treating April 2026 as the final word.
No current, authoritative square footage or cost figure exists for the project as of this record's last_verified date: the 2022 estimates are explicitly being re-evaluated under the 2026 Amended ENA.

No public official's or community/maritime-advocacy group's position on the 2026 Amended ENA or settlement specifically has been found and sourced (all community-input coverage found dates to the 2020 RFP era).

Given the project's history of default and its ongoing, unresolved Evaluation Period, its ultimate outcome is genuinely uncertain -- this record treats it as an active but fragile project worth continued tracking, not a settled one.

names: 22nd Street Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement
records.distance_note: The existing 22nd St Caltrain station (Pennsylvania Ave/Indiana St, Dogpatch) sits roughly 400-450m from both Pier 70's and Potrero Power Station's tracked boundaries -- grouped here under Pier 70 as the closer, better-established Dogpatch association.

how_to_comment.channel: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain) meeting calendar

records.summary: An accessibility retrofit of the existing, below-grade 22nd Street Caltrain station -- the only regular-service Caltrain station without wheelchair access. The project adds ramps to both platforms plus wayfinding and safety improvements. Design is under way (targeted complete summer 2027); construction is not slated to start until spring 2028, with completion targeted for mid-2029. Total project cost is $19,134,000, sponsored by the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain) with SFCTA (Prop L) and FTA funding.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a coarse placeholder box over the existing station's real location, not a traced footprint of the platforms or the planned ramps themselves (one ~305ft ramp on the northbound platform, one ~465ft ramp on the southbound platform, per the project's own design description).
notes.digitized_from: No Assessor block/lot exists for the existing 22nd St Caltrain station or its below-grade platforms (active rail right-of-way, the same reasoning already documented for the nearby 4th & King Station in the Mission Bay railyards record -- confirmed here too: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' Socrata dataset has no parcel at this location). No Caltrain/Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board GIS shapefile or site-plan figure was available, so this is a coarse locational box near the real DataSF street-centerline address range for 22nd St at Pennsylvania Ave/Indiana St (DataSF's official street centerlines), where the existing below-grade station sits.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Active Caltrain rail right-of-way; not on the Assessor's secured roll, the same situation as the existing 4th & King Street Station (mapped in Pier & Point's Mission Bay railyards record).
notes.regulatory_context: The Caltrain 22nd Street Station is the railroad's only regular-service station that is not wheelchair accessible: its platforms sit about 25 ft below street level, reachable only by stairs. Sponsor: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain); funded in part through SFCTA's Prop L. Total project cost per SFCTA's April 2026 Board Packet: $19,134,000 (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L, allocated 2026-04-28; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design). The FTA's 'All Stations Accessibility Program' separately awarded the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board $14.1 million for this project's ADA improvements, announced 2026-09-10 -- matching almost exactly the funding gap SFCTA's own April 2026 plan had left as 'Planned TBD'.

facts.value: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain), with funding from SFCTA (Prop L) and the FTA
